body:
**Task ID:** `t2099` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~45m`
**Logged:** 2026-04-14
**Tags:** `feat` `community` `auto-dispatch` `interactive`

## Description

feat(issue-sync): auto-apply good first issue label to tier:simple issues — extend _apply_tier_label_replace in issue-sync-helper.sh so whenever tier:simple is applied, the good first issue label is also ensured via gh_create_label and added. Only added on tier:simple, never auto-removed on escalation (label is already in _is_protected_label and may reflect human intent). Surfaces prescriptive single-file pattern-follow tasks to GitHub standard community discovery filters. Adds test assertion and one-line AGENTS.md note. Backfill open tier:simple issues across pulse repos after merge.

## Worker Guidance


### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh` — extend `_apply_tier_label_replace` to also add `good first issue` when the new tier is `tier:simple`.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-tier-extraction.sh` — add assertion that applying `tier:simple` triggers `--add-label good first issue`.
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` — one-line note on the `tier:simple` bullet that `good first issue` is auto-applied.

### Reference pattern

Model on the existing `_apply_tier_label_replace` flow (`.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh:132-168`). The final `gh issue edit … --add-label "$new_tier"` line is the extension point — append the `good first issue` ensure-and-add step immediately after, gated on `[[ "$new_tier" == "tier:simple" ]]`.

Use `gh_create_label` (already defined at `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh:255-258`) to ensure the label exists before adding it — it is idempotent via `--force`.

```bash
.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-tier-extraction.sh
```

## Task Brief

# t2099: auto-apply `good first issue` label to `tier:simple` issues

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-04-14
- **Session:** claude:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** User asked to have every issue tagged `tier:simple` also carry GitHub's community `good first issue` label, then full-loop through to merge.

## What

When `_apply_tier_label_replace` in `issue-sync-helper.sh` applies `tier:simple` to an issue, it must also add the `good first issue` label (creating the label first if it does not exist on the target repo). The label is ONLY added on `tier:simple` — it is never auto-removed when a task later escalates to `tier:standard`/`tier:thinking`, because `good first issue` is already in the `_is_protected_label` set and may have been added by a human.

After shipping, backfill all currently-open `tier:simple` issues across `pulse: true` repos so the label applies retroactively.

## Why

`tier:simple` issues are, by definition, prescriptive single-file pattern-follows with verbatim code blocks — the exact shape of a community-friendly first contribution. Surfacing them via GitHub's standard `good first issue` label exposes them to the built-in GitHub "good first issues" filter and third-party discovery sites (goodfirstissue.dev, up-for-grabs, code-triage). We already produce this pool mechanically; we just were not labelling it for external discovery.

## Tier

### Tier checklist

- [x] 2 or fewer files to modify? (issue-sync-helper.sh + test file; AGENTS.md pointer is a 1-line doc touch)
- [x] Complete code blocks for every edit?
- [x] No judgment or design decisions?
- [x] No error handling or fallback logic to design?
- [x] Estimate 1h or less?
- [x] 4 or fewer acceptance criteria?

**Selected tier:** `tier:simple`

**Tier rationale:** Single-function append in one helper, one test assertion block, one doc pointer. Verbatim code blocks below.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh` — extend `_apply_tier_label_replace` to also add `good first issue` when the new tier is `tier:simple`.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-tier-extraction.sh` — add assertion that applying `tier:simple` triggers `--add-label good first issue`.
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` — one-line note on the `tier:simple` bullet that `good first issue` is auto-applied.

### Reference pattern

Model on the existing `_apply_tier_label_replace` flow (`.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh:132-168`). The final `gh issue edit … --add-label "$new_tier"` line is the extension point — append the `good first issue` ensure-and-add step immediately after, gated on `[[ "$new_tier" == "tier:simple" ]]`.

Use `gh_create_label` (already defined at `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh:255-258`) to ensure the label exists before adding it — it is idempotent via `--force`.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-tier-extraction.sh
```

All existing tier-extraction tests must continue to pass; a new assertion must pass proving `good first issue` is added on `tier:simple`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_apply_tier_label_replace` adds `good first issue` when (and only when) `new_tier == tier:simple`
- [ ] Label is ensured to exist via `gh_create_label` before `--add-label`
- [ ] Test `test-issue-sync-tier-extraction.sh` asserts the new behaviour and all prior tests pass
- [ ] PR merged (closes #19007) and existing open `tier:simple` issues backfilled across pulse repos

## Context

- `_is_protected_label` already protects `good first issue` from tag-derived reconciliation, so the label survives once applied.
- `gh_create_label` uses `--force` and silently succeeds if the label already exists.
- No removal on escalation: keeps logic simple and avoids fighting human intent.

title: GraphQL budget optimisation roadmap — scale to 50+ repos
body:
## Context

GH#18976 (GraphQL rate-limit exhaustion in pulse prefetch) is resolved:
- **t2097** (PR #18983): fail-loud on rate-limit detection + cycle abort
- **t2098** (PR #18985): idle repo skip — reuse cached data on cache-hit

Current state (v3.8.30): ~3800 GraphQL calls/hr observed during heavy dispatch with 14 repos. Budget is 5000/hr. Headroom is adequate but thin during peak worker activity. Scaling to 50+ repos will require further optimisation.

This issue tracks investigation items to revisit once we have more production data from the t2097/t2098 changes. **Do not implement without measurements.**

## Optimisation candidates (gather data first)

### 1. Worker-side `gh` call reduction
Each dispatched worker makes its own `gh` calls: `gh issue view`, `gh pr create`, `gh pr checks` polling, `gh pr merge`, closing comments. During heavy dispatch (10+ concurrent workers), this is the dominant consumer — not prefetch.

**Data to gather**: instrument or log-sample worker-side `gh` call counts per session. Identify which calls are redundant (e.g., polling checks every 30s when CI takes 3+ min).

**Potential fixes**: longer poll intervals for checks, pass prefetched issue body to worker via env/file instead of re-fetching, batch merge-summary comments.

### 2. Adaptive cycle frequency
Currently all repos run on the same pulse cycle (~10 min). Active repos (aidevops, <webapp>) need frequent cycles; idle repos (10+ with 0 PRs) could run every 30-60 min without losing responsiveness.

**Data to gather**: per-repo dispatch frequency from logs. How often does an idle repo actually get dispatched?

**Potential fix**: tier repos by activity level, run idle repos every Nth cycle. The idle skip (t2098) already skips expensive calls — this would skip the cheap ones too (fingerprint + delta check = 4 calls per idle repo).

### 3. Conditional NMR/needs-info full scan
The `_prefetch_cached_label_count_is_zero` helper (t2098) skips repos with 0 cached matching issues. But when a repo DOES have matching issues, it still makes a full `gh issue list --label X` call every cycle even if the cached data hasn't changed. A delta approach (check `updatedAt` before re-fetching) would save 1-2 calls per active repo per cycle.

**Data to gather**: how often do NMR/needs-info issue lists actually change between cycles?

### 4. REST API for read-heavy, write-light paths
The original REST fallback proposal (GH#18976) was deferred due to 6 risks. Some of those risks apply only to the main dispatch pipeline. Read-only paths (daily cap count, NMR scan, needs-info scan) could safely use REST without field-mapping or dedup concerns. This preserves GraphQL budget for the dispatch-critical paths (PR list with `reviewDecision`, issue list with full labels).

**Data to gather**: what percentage of GraphQL budget is consumed by read-only auxiliary paths vs dispatch-critical paths?

### 5. GitHub App installation for higher rate limits
A GitHub App installation gets 5000 REST + 5000 GraphQL calls/hr per installation (not per user). If the pulse ran under an App token, it would double the effective budget without any code optimisation.

**Data to gather**: is the complexity of App token management worth the budget doubling? Only relevant if the above optimisations are insufficient.

## Decision criteria

Implement the cheapest option that keeps GraphQL consumption below 60% of budget (3000/hr) at the target repo count. Measure before and after. No speculative optimisation.

## Prior work

- GH#18976 — investigation + fixes (closed)
- PR #18983 (t2097) — fail-loud detection
- PR #18985 (t2098) — idle repo skip
- GH#15286 — delta prefetch cache (original)
- t2041 — state fingerprint cache-hit detection

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #18787 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #18787

**Parent issue:** #18787 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** t2076: feat(tooling): add static scanner for unguarded Linux/macOS-only command calls in shell scripts
**Parent labels:** `enhancement,auto-dispatch,status:queued,bash-compat,origin:interactive,origin:worker,tier:standard,tooling`

> You do **NOT** need to read #18787. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #18787 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**


## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #18787** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

## Parent body (verbatim)

## What

Add a static scanner that greps all `.sh` files in the repo for unguarded calls to Linux-only commands (getent, readlink -f, stat --format, date -d, sed -r, grep -P, timeout, sha256sum, base64 -w, find -printf, xargs -r, mktemp --suffix) and macOS-only commands (dscl, sw_vers, launchctl, pbcopy, defaults, security, codesign), and fails CI if any unguarded usage is found.

## Why

PR #18785 (t2074, GH#18784) added a comprehensive table of cross-platform command divergences to `.agents/reference/bash-compat.md`, but the rules are documentation-only — there is no automated enforcement. Three production bugs in the same week were all caused by unguarded command calls that would have been caught by a grep-based scanner:

- **GH#18784** — `getent passwd` unguarded in `aidevops.sh`, broke macOS
- **GH#18770** — `_pulse_handle_self_check` set-e propagation (adjacent bug class, same pre-merge checklist)
- **t1983 (GH#18423)** — BSD awk dynamic-regex construct silently broke on macOS

The guarded pattern is easy to detect:
- Unguarded: `getent passwd ...`
- Guarded: `command -v getent &>/dev/null && getent passwd ...` OR preceded by `[[ "$(uname)" == "Linux" ]]`

## How

Create `.agents/scripts/lint-shell-portability.sh` that:

1. Enumerates all tracked `.sh` files via `git ls-files "*.sh"` (excluding `tests/` optionally).
2. For each file, scans for each Linux-only/macOS-only command pattern from the table in `.agents/reference/bash-compat.md`.
3. For each hit, verifies the same physical line or the 3-5 preceding lines contain one of:
   - `command -v <cmd>` guard
   - `[[ "$(uname)" == "Darwin" ]]` or `[[ "$(uname)" == "Linux" ]]` branch
   - An already-portable wrapper name (from the "canonical portable wrappers" table in bash-compat.md)
4. Emits one error per unguarded hit with `file:line: unguarded <cmd>` format.
5. Returns non-zero if any errors.

Then add a CI job `.github/workflows/shell-portability.yml` that runs the scanner on PR changes (or full scan on main push) and blocks merge on failure.

### Scanner design notes

- **Use rg, not grep** — `rg` has faster startup and better file-type filtering.
- **Patterns should be regex-anchored** — `\bgetent\s+passwd\b` not just `getent`, to avoid matching comments/strings.
- **Allow an inline suppression** — comment marker `# shell-portability: ignore next` for the rare legitimate case.
- **Don't scan `bash-compat.md` or the scanner itself** — they contain the patterns as documentation.
- **Test the scanner** with a fixture file that deliberately contains both guarded and unguarded usages, assert the scanner flags the unguarded ones and passes the guarded ones.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.agents/scripts/lint-shell-portability.sh` exists and is executable
- [ ] Scanner finds the exact bug pattern from GH#18784 when run against the pre-fix `aidevops.sh` (regression-style test)
- [ ] Scanner passes cleanly on current main
- [ ] Fixture-based unit test in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-lint-shell-portability.sh` covering 5+ guarded and 5+ unguarded examples
- [ ] `.github/workflows/shell-portability.yml` runs the scanner on PRs
- [ ] `linters-local.sh` includes the scanner in its local-run list so developers catch issues before push

## Context

- Precedent: `.agents/reference/bash-compat.md` (PR #18785) — the full pattern table
- Adjacent work: `prompts/build.txt` → "ShellCheck zero violations" already exists as a separate rule; this extends the quality bar to coreutils portability
- Related bug class: set -e + function return code capture (3 prod hits in one week: GH#18770, GH#18784, GH#18786). A second lint rule could catch `$(f); local rc=$?` without a preceding `|| has_rc=$?` — tracked separately if this PR grows too large.

body:
## Agent doc simplification (automated scan)

**File:** `.agents/workflows/brief/templates.md`
**Detected topic:** Brief Composition Templates
**Current size:** 140 lines

### Classify before acting

**First, determine the file type** — the correct action depends on whether this is an instruction doc or a reference corpus:

- **Instruction doc** (agent rules, workflows, decision trees, operational procedures): Tighten prose, reorder by importance, split if multiple concerns. Follow guidance below.
- **Reference corpus** (SKILL.md, domain knowledge base, textbook-style content with self-contained sections): Do NOT compress content. Instead, split into chapter files with a slim index. See `tools/code-review/code-simplifier.md` "Reference corpora" classification (GH#6432).

### For instruction docs — proposed action

Tighten and restructure this agent doc. Follow `tools/build-agent/build-agent.md` guidance. Key principles:

1. **Preserve all institutional knowledge** — every verbose rule exists because something broke without it. Do not remove task IDs, incident references, error statistics, or decision rationale. Compress prose, not knowledge.
2. **Order by importance** — most critical instructions first (primacy effect: LLMs weight earlier context more heavily). Security rules, core workflow, then edge cases.
3. **Split if needed** — if the file covers multiple distinct concerns, extract sub-docs with a parent index. Use progressive disclosure (pointers, not inline content).
4. **Use search patterns, not line numbers** — any `file:line_number` references to other files go stale on every edit. Use `rg "pattern"` or section heading references instead.

### For reference corpora — proposed action

1. **Extract each major section** into its own file (e.g., `01-introduction.md`, `02-fundamentals.md`)
2. **Replace the original with a slim index** (~100-200 lines) — table of contents with one-line descriptions and file pointers
3. **Zero content loss** — every line moves to a chapter file, nothing is deleted or compressed
4. **Reconcile existing chapter files** — if partial splits already exist, deduplicate and keep the most complete version

### Verification

- Content preservation: all code blocks, URLs, task ID references (`tNNN`, `GH#NNN`), and command examples must be present before and after
- No broken internal links or references
- Agent behaviour unchanged (test with a representative query if possible)
- Qlty smells resolved for the target file: `~/.qlty/bin/qlty smells --all 2>&1 | grep '.agents/workflows/brief/templates.md' | grep -c . | grep -q '^0$'` (report `SKIP` if Qlty is unavailable, not `FAIL`)
- For reference corpora: `wc -l` total of chapter files >= original line count minus index overhead

### Confidence: medium

Automated scan flagged this file for maintainer review. The best simplification strategy requires human judgment — some files are appropriately structured already. Reference corpora (SKILL.md, domain knowledge bases) need restructuring into chapters, not content reduction.

title: t2103: feat(pulse): pre-dispatch no-op validator for auto-generated issues
body:
**Task ID:** `t2103` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~3h`
**Logged:** 2026-04-15
**Tags:** `enhancement` `pulse` `auto-dispatch` `interactive`

## Outcome

feat(pulse): pre-dispatch no-op validator for auto-generated issues — new `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh` with a `validate <issue> <slug>` subcommand that runs a registered validator for the issue's generator type in a fresh checkout before spawning a worker. Exit 0=dispatch, 10=falsified+close, 20=validator-error+warn+dispatch. First validator: ratchet-down (runs `complexity-scan-helper.sh ratchet-check . 5`, returns 10 on "No ratchet-down available"). Generator identification via hidden body marker `<!-- aidevops:generator=ratchet-down -->`. Defense-in-depth layer — workers ignored "Worker triage responsibility" prompt rule on #19024, so moving the check before dispatch makes it deterministic. Extensible to quality-debt, review-followup, contribution-watch as follow-ups. Requires research to find the right dispatch hook point. New helper + new test harness + docs in `reference/pre-dispatch-validators.md`.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn -->

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-04-15
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** marcusquinn (ai-interactive)
- **Parent task:** t2100 / #19035
- **Conversation context:** Fix 3 of the #19024 post-mortem — the defense-in-depth layer. Fixes 1 and 2 (#19036, #19037) eliminate the ratchet-down bug at the source; this fix adds a generalisable safety net that catches the same class of failure for any future auto-generated issue type.

## What

New helper `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh` with a `validate <issue-number> <slug>` subcommand. Before the pulse spawns a worker for an auto-generated issue, this runs a registered validator for that issue's generator type in a fresh checkout. Exit codes:

- `0` = dispatch proceeds
- `10` = premise falsified, caller closes the issue with a rationale comment instead of dispatching
- `20` = validator error, dispatch proceeds with a warning log

First concrete validator: **ratchet-down**. Runs `complexity-scan-helper.sh ratchet-check . 5` in a fresh clone and returns exit 10 if it reports "No ratchet-down available".

Generator identification uses a hidden body marker `<!-- aidevops:generator=ratchet-down -->` that the issue generator in `_complexity_scan_ratchet_check` must emit. Generator-marker extraction is safer than parsing titles or labels.

## Why

The #19024 worker silently exited despite the explicit "Worker triage responsibility" prompt rule. Prompt-following failures cannot be robustly fixed with more prompt text. Moving the no-op check before dispatch makes it deterministic — the pulse doesn't rely on the model.

Once ratchet-down is in place, the mechanism extends to quality-debt, review-followup, and contribution-watch generators as separate follow-ups. The extensibility pattern is "one validator script per generator, registered at startup", not "extract commands from issue bodies".

## Tier

**tier:standard** — new helper + new mechanism + new test harness + dispatch-engine integration. Requires research to identify the right dispatch hook point. ~2-3h estimate. Not tier:simple because it touches multiple files and introduces a new abstraction.

## Reference

- Parent: #19035
- Incident: #19024
- Full design, file list, research steps, and acceptance criteria in the GitHub issue body at **#19038**
- Worker prompt rule that was ignored: `prompts/build.txt` "Worker triage responsibility (GH#18538)"

## Acceptance

- `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh` helper with `validate` subcommand
- Ratchet-down validator registered and tested (falsified and legitimate cases)
- Dispatch entry-point calls validator after dedup, before worker spawn
- Generator marker `<!-- aidevops:generator=ratchet-down -->` emitted by `_complexity_scan_ratchet_check`
- Exit 10 triggers issue closure with rationale + signature footer
- Emergency bypass env var `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PREDISPATCH_VALIDATOR=1`
- Documentation: `reference/pre-dispatch-validators.md`
- Test coverage: ratchet-down falsified, ratchet-down legitimate, unregistered generator fallback
- No regression on legitimate ratchet-down dispatches

## Non-goals

- Don't implement validators for other generator types in this issue
- Don't extract commands from issue bodies at runtime (injection surface)
- Don't block dispatch on validator errors (log and proceed)

title: t2104: pulse-merge: filter required-only checks via gh pr checks --required to eliminate post-merge/advisory false positives
body:
## What

Refine `_pr_required_checks_pass` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` so the deterministic merge pass only considers branch-protection-required checks. Replace the current `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup` jq filter with `gh pr checks <PR> --required --json bucket` which returns only checks that are required by branch protection.

## Why

Current implementation fetches `statusCheckRollup` and counts ANY `FAILURE`/`TIMED_OUT` conclusion. This includes:

1. **Post-merge workflows** (e.g., `Sync Issue Hygiene on PR Merge` which runs on push to main and is expected to fail under the documented t2029 limitation — github-actions[bot] cannot push to protected main on personal repos)
2. **Advisory / non-required checks** — checks not in branch protection that happen to attach to the PR head

**Concrete regression (GH#18787 / PR #19023):**

- 23:52:10Z — Qlty Smell Regression failed on commit `c964794` (ratchet-bump label not yet applied)
- 23:55:45Z — Pulse merge pass ran, saw `c964794` still failing → skipped #19023 correctly at this point
- 23:58:01Z — Worker pushed commit `40ff76e` (ratchet-bump re-trigger)
- 23:58:41Z — Qlty Smell Regression **passed** on `40ff76e`
- 23:58 – 00:07 — No further pulse merge pass successfully processed #19023
- 00:07:09Z — Manual maintainer intervention required

On inspection, the PR head (`40ff76e`) had **every required check passing** but the `Sync Issue Hygiene on PR Merge` post-merge workflow was present in `statusCheckRollup` with `conclusion: FAILURE`. Even without the timing issue, this post-merge workflow would keep blocking the gate permanently — because `_pr_required_checks_pass` doesn't distinguish required from advisory checks.

Root cause: `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup` returns ALL check runs attached to the PR head commit, including post-merge workflow runs triggered by the merge itself (on the merge commit), advisory checks outside branch protection, and stale entries. The jq filter has no way to tell which ones are required.

## How

Replace the body of `_pr_required_checks_pass` (currently at `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh:660-681`) to use `gh pr checks` with the `--required` flag:

```bash
failing=$(gh pr checks "$pr_number" --repo "$repo_slug" --required --json bucket \
    --jq '[.[] | select(.bucket == "fail" or .bucket == "cancel")] | length' \
    2>/dev/null)
```

- `--required`: returns only checks required by branch protection
- `bucket` field: `pass`, `fail`, `pending`, `cancel`, `skipping`
- Count only `fail` and `cancel` as blocking (preserves old semantics: `pending` → allow via `--admin`, `skipping` → not an error)
- Empty array (no required checks defined) → zero failures → merge allowed

**Log message**: update wording to reference \"required status check(s)\" so the meaning is explicit in `pulse.log`.

**Fail-closed behaviour on API errors**: preserve the existing semantic — if `gh pr checks` exits non-zero, skip the merge. A bubbling GH API error should never auto-merge.

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` — `_pr_required_checks_pass()` function body (~20 lines)
- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-required-checks-filter.sh` — 4+ unit tests via mocked `gh` binary on `PATH`

### Test cases

1. **Post-merge failure ignored** — mock `gh pr checks --required --json bucket` returning `[{\"bucket\":\"pass\"},{\"bucket\":\"pass\"}]` (post-merge `Sync Issue Hygiene` workflow is NOT in the required set → not returned). Assert function returns 0 (merge allowed).
2. **Required failure blocks** — mock returning `[{\"bucket\":\"pass\"},{\"bucket\":\"fail\"}]`. Assert function returns 1 and log contains \"1 required status check(s)\".
3. **No required checks** — mock returning `[]`. Assert function returns 0.
4. **Pending required check** — mock returning `[{\"bucket\":\"pending\"}]`. Assert function returns 0 (allow via --admin, matches old semantic).
5. **gh API error** — mock `gh` exits 1. Assert function returns 1 (fail-closed).

Follow the mock-gh pattern from `test-pulse-merge-parent-task-close-guard.sh`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_pr_required_checks_pass` uses `gh pr checks --required --json bucket`
- [ ] New test file with 5 cases passes
- [ ] `shellcheck` clean on edited file
- [ ] `linters-local.sh` full run clean
- [ ] No regression in `test-pulse-merge-parent-task-close-guard.sh`, `test-pulse-merge-fix-worker-dispatch.sh`, `test-pulse-merge-rebase-nudge.sh`
- [ ] Comment in `_pr_required_checks_pass` references this issue

## Context

- Previous fix: t2092 (GH#18962, PR #18968) added the current `_pr_required_checks_pass` gate — this issue refines it without reverting its intent
- t2029 known limitation (AGENTS.md): `sync-on-pr-merge` can't push to protected main on personal repos → `Sync Issue Hygiene on PR Merge` is **expected to fail** and must not block merges
- Related resilience issues (out of scope here but tracked separately): pulse FD exhaustion, watchdog SIGTERM killing merge pass cycles

title: t2105: fix(cli): wire `aidevops issue` subcommand to interactive-session-helper.sh
body:

**Logged:** 2026-04-15
**Tags:** `bug` `tooling` `auto-dispatch` `interactive`

## Description

fix(cli): wire `aidevops issue` subcommand to interactive-session-helper.sh — `prompts/build.txt` and `.agents/AGENTS.md` document `aidevops issue release <N>` as a fallback for releasing stale interactive claims, but the subcommand is not in the `aidevops.sh` dispatch table. Calling it falls through to the help text. Discovered live on 2026-04-15 while releasing a stale claim on #18768 during the t2053.1 session. Two-line fix: add `issue) _dispatch_helper "interactive-session-helper.sh" ...` after the `approve)` case at `aidevops.sh:3861`, and a matching one-line entry in `cmd_help()` at `aidevops.sh:3514`. Helper already implements claim/release/status/scan-stale; this is plumbing only.

## Task Brief

<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->

# t2105 — wire `aidevops issue` CLI subcommand

**Issue:** GH#19042
**Tier:** `tier:simple` (Haiku)
**Origin:** interactive (Marcus, 2026-04-15, post-t2053.1 session)
**Estimate:** 20 min

## What

Add an `issue)` case to the `aidevops` CLI dispatch table that forwards to `interactive-session-helper.sh`, exposing `claim`, `release`, `status`, and `scan-stale` as `aidevops issue <subcommand>`. Also add the new subcommand to the help text. Then verify with a runtime smoke test against a closed issue.

This is plumbing only. The implementation already exists in `interactive-session-helper.sh` — the helper supports `claim <issue> <slug>`, `release <issue> <slug> [--unassign]`, `status [<issue>]`, and `scan-stale`. The CLI is just a thin pass-through dispatcher (same pattern as 30+ other subcommands in `aidevops.sh`).

## Why

`prompts/build.txt` and `.agents/AGENTS.md` both document `aidevops issue release <N>` as a fallback path for releasing stale interactive claims. The documentation has shipped for at least t2056 (the introduction of the interactive-session-helper). The CLI was never wired up — calling `aidevops issue release 18768` today falls through to `Unknown command` and prints the help text. Discovered live on 2026-04-15 while releasing a stale claim on #18768 during the t2053.1 session.

The mismatch is small but actively misleading: documentation tells operators a command exists, the command silently no-ops by hitting the help fallback, and the user has to know to dig out `interactive-session-helper.sh release` from `.agents/scripts/` to actually do the thing.

## How

### File 1: `aidevops.sh` — add dispatch case

Find the existing dispatch line for `approve` (around **line 3861**, inside the `case "$command" in` block in `main()`):

```bash
	approve) _dispatch_helper "approval-helper.sh" "approval-helper.sh" "$@" ;;
```

Add the new case **immediately after it**, on its own line, using the same `_dispatch_helper` pattern that every other subcommand uses:

```bash
	issue) _dispatch_helper "interactive-session-helper.sh" "interactive-session-helper.sh" "$@" ;;
```

That's the entire dispatch wiring. `_dispatch_helper` (defined at line 3710) handles the path resolution between `$AGENTS_DIR/scripts/` (deployed) and `$INSTALL_DIR/.agents/scripts/` (repo). Pass-through `"$@"` forwards every argument, so `aidevops issue release 18768 marcusquinn/aidevops --unassign` becomes `interactive-session-helper.sh release 18768 marcusquinn/aidevops --unassign` exactly.

### File 2: `aidevops.sh` — add help line

Find the existing help line for `approve` in `cmd_help()` (around **line 3514**):

```bash
	echo "  approve <cmd>      Cryptographic issue/PR approval (setup/issue/pr/verify/status)"
```

Add the new help line **immediately after it**, matching the column alignment used by every other entry in this block (subcommand name padded to 19 characters, then description):

```bash
	echo "  issue <cmd>        Interactive issue ownership (claim/release/status/scan-stale)"
```

Do not touch `_help_detailed_sections()` or any other help function — the one-line entry in the main `cmd_help()` block is what gets printed by `aidevops` with no args and `aidevops --help`.

### Verification

Run from the worktree, in this exact order:

```bash
# 1. ShellCheck the file you edited
shellcheck aidevops.sh

# 2. Confirm the new command appears in help output
bash aidevops.sh help | grep "issue <cmd>"
# Expected: one matching line

# 3. Confirm the dispatch reaches the helper (--help is a safe read-only call)
bash aidevops.sh issue 2>&1 | grep "interactive-session-helper.sh"
# Expected: the helper's USAGE banner mentioning interactive-session-helper.sh

# 4. Smoke test against a closed issue (release is idempotent and safe on a clean state)
bash aidevops.sh issue status 18768
# Expected: the helper's status output, NOT the aidevops CLI help text

# 5. Confirm the helper's release path is reachable end-to-end
#    (no-op on an issue without status:in-review — the helper handles this gracefully)
bash aidevops.sh issue release 18768 marcusquinn/aidevops
# Expected: "[interactive-session] release: #18768 not in status:in-review — no-op"
#           or "[interactive-session] release: #18768 → status:available"
#           Either is acceptable. NEITHER should be the aidevops CLI Unknown-command fallback.
```

If any of steps 2–5 fall through to `Unknown command: issue` or print the aidevops CLI help block, the wiring is wrong — re-check that the new `issue)` line is inside the `case "$command" in` block (not outside it) and uses a single-line format with the trailing `;;`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `aidevops issue release <N> <slug>` reaches `interactive-session-helper.sh release <N> <slug>` (verifiable via step 5 above).
2. `aidevops issue status` and `aidevops issue scan-stale` reach the helper's corresponding subcommands (same pass-through).
3. `aidevops help` shows the new `issue <cmd>` line in the main subcommand listing.
4. `shellcheck aidevops.sh` is clean (no new violations).

## Out of scope

- **Changing `interactive-session-helper.sh`** — the helper already has the implementation. Do not touch it.
- **Adding new subcommands** beyond what the helper exposes. If the helper grows new subcommands later, the pass-through inherits them automatically.
- **Updating `_help_detailed_sections()`** with a verbose `aidevops issue ...` example block. The one-line entry in `cmd_help()` is sufficient and matches the convention of `approve`, `secret`, `config`, etc.
- **Removing the `/release-issue` slash command** if it exists. Both fallbacks should coexist.

title: t2106: fix(pulse): resolve FD exhaustion + watchdog SIGTERM killing merge pass cycles
body:
## What

Pulse cycles are being terminated before completing the deterministic merge pass, causing worker PRs to sit unmerged even when all required checks are green. Two symptoms observed in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log`:

1. **FD exhaustion** — `pulse-simplification-state.sh: redirection error: cannot duplicate fd: Too many open files` appearing repeatedly across multiple pulse cycles
2. **Watchdog SIGTERM** — `pulse-watchdog.sh: line 184: <pid> Terminated: 15 "$@"` killing pulse processes mid-cycle

Effect: `deterministic_merge_pass` stage never runs for affected cycles, worker PRs accumulate in `REVIEW_REQUIRED` + all-green state until a human notices.

## Why

Investigated in context of GH#18787 / PR #19023 (worker-authored PR with all required checks green, sat for ~9 minutes before manual intervention). The complementary t2104 fix (GH#19040, PR #19041) resolved the check-filtering false-positive that triggered the skip, but the deeper issue is that even when the merge pass WOULD succeed, pulse isn't reliably reaching it.

**Evidence from pulse-wrapper.log** (GH#18787 timeframe, ~01:08 UTC 2026-04-15):

```text
[pulse-wrapper] Instance lock acquired via mkdir (PID 82964)
pulse-watchdog.sh: line 184: 83555 Terminated: 15 "$@"
[pulse-wrapper] Instance lock acquired via mkdir (PID 95734)
pulse-simplification-state.sh: redirection error: cannot duplicate fd: Too many open files
```

Two cycles back-to-back, both truncated. The merge pass line 4477 ("Stage start: deterministic_merge_pass") only appeared ONCE in the log across the whole incident window — the subsequent cycles that should have retried PR #19023 simply died before reaching that stage.

## How

This task is intentionally **tier:thinking** because the root cause analysis needs to come before the fix — it could be any of (or a combination of):

1. **FD leak in `pulse-simplification-state.sh`** — script opens files in a loop without closing them, or uses `exec` redirects that accumulate across iterations
2. **Process-level `ulimit -n` too low** — pulse runs under launchd with a default soft limit that's insufficient once subprocess count grows
3. **FD inheritance across `|` pipes and `$( )` subshells** — fds opened in outer shell inherited by children that never close them (bash 3.2 pattern)
4. **Watchdog timeout mismatch** — `pulse-watchdog.sh` killing cycles before they legitimately finish a slow merge pass, especially when merge pass itself waits on `gh pr list` for 14 repos

Dependency: the investigator must run the pulse long enough to reproduce the symptom (can't be solved from logs alone in 30 minutes), correlate FD usage with subprocess count, and decide whether the fix is:

- (a) Plug the specific leak in `pulse-simplification-state.sh`
- (b) Raise `ulimit -n` in the launchd plist (`~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse.plist`)
- (c) Redesign the watchdog's timeout budget to account for slow merge passes
- (d) Some combination

### Files to investigate

- **`.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-state.sh`** — the script emitting the FD errors. Audit every `<`, `>`, `exec`, `</dev/null`, and loop-contained redirect for leaks.
- **`.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh:184`** — the SIGTERM site. Understand which pulse process is being killed, why, and whether the timeout is proportional to the merge pass workload.
- **`~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse.plist`** — check `SoftResourceLimits` / `HardResourceLimits` for NumberOfFiles. Default macOS launchd is 256 — almost certainly too low for a pulse that spawns `gh` per repo × per PR.
- **`.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`** — the main cycle orchestrator. Does it set `ulimit -n` itself before launching subprocesses?

### Investigation approach

1. Reproduce by running the pulse manually with `strace`/`dtruss` (macOS) to capture FD usage over one cycle
2. `lsof -p <pulse-pid>` snapshots at start, mid-merge-pass, and end
3. Check `sysctl kern.maxfiles` and `launchctl limit maxfiles` baseline
4. Once root cause confirmed: implement the minimal fix, add a regression guard (e.g., `pulse-wrapper.sh` asserts `ulimit -n >= 1024` at start)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Root cause identified and documented (FD leak vs ulimit vs watchdog vs combination)
- [ ] Fix implemented in the appropriate file(s)
- [ ] Regression guard added: pulse fails loudly if FD budget is insufficient at cycle start, so future regressions are visible instead of silent
- [ ] `pulse.log` shows `deterministic_merge_pass` stage reaching completion for every cycle over a 30-minute observation window after the fix
- [ ] Test or log-assertion documenting the expected FD baseline

## Context

- Related: t2104 (GH#19040 / PR #19041) — the check-filtering fix that made pulse's merge pass less over-eager on skips. Complementary but independent.
- Related: t2029 — known `sync-on-pr-merge` branch protection limitation that triggers the post-merge workflow failure the old gate was reacting to.
- Session transcript: the t2104 investigation in session "a6ad2ada-97a3-4533-b74f-c70bb8eecb36" contains the full diagnostic evidence

title: t2107: fix(ci): trigger qlty-regression on `pull_request.labeled` so ratchet-bump re-runs without empty commits
body:
## What

Add `pull_request.labeled` to the trigger list of `.github/workflows/qlty-regression.yml` so applying the `ratchet-bump` label automatically re-runs the Qlty Smell Regression check, instead of requiring the worker to push an empty "trigger" commit.

## Why

When a worker's PR fails Qlty Smell Regression because the PR introduces a net increase in smells for legitimate reasons (intentional code trade-off), the documented override is to apply the `ratchet-bump` label. Problem: today the workflow doesn't listen for `labeled` events, so applying the label is a no-op until the next push. Workers work around this by pushing empty commits:

```
commit 93febaef... ci: trigger re-run after ratchet-bump label [no-op]
commit 40ff76eb6... ci: trigger re-run with ratchet-bump label applied
```

Observed in PR #19023 (GH#18787) — the worker pushed **two** empty commits trying to get CI to re-evaluate with the label applied. Each empty commit re-triggers the whole check suite (wasteful), and creates a window during which `statusCheckRollup` is stale and other gates (like the pre-t2104 merge pass) misfire.

## How

Edit `.github/workflows/qlty-regression.yml` — add `labeled` to the `pull_request.types` array so the workflow fires whenever a label is added:

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled]
```

The existing job logic already reads `github.event.pull_request.labels` / checks for `ratchet-bump`, so no job-level changes are needed — the trigger addition is sufficient.

**Guard (optional, nice-to-have)**: inside the job, early-exit with success when `github.event.action == 'labeled'` AND `github.event.label.name != 'ratchet-bump'`. This avoids re-running the full Qlty scan when an unrelated label (e.g. `origin:worker`, `status:in-review`) is applied. Without this guard the workflow re-runs on every label add, which is wasteful but not incorrect.

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.github/workflows/qlty-regression.yml` — add `labeled` to `on.pull_request.types`, and optionally add the label-name guard in the job

### Verification

1. Create a throwaway PR with a deliberate smell increase → Qlty Smell Regression fails
2. Apply the `ratchet-bump` label (no push) → workflow re-runs automatically and reports success
3. Apply an unrelated label → workflow either skips (with guard) or re-runs and reports whatever state matches the current code (without guard)

Apply the same fix to the `Qlty New-File Smell Gate` workflow (`.github/workflows/qlty-new-file-gate.yml`) if it has an equivalent `new-file-smell-ok` label override — same rationale.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `on.pull_request.types` in qlty-regression.yml includes `labeled`
- [ ] Applying `ratchet-bump` to an already-failing PR re-runs the check without needing a new commit
- [ ] Optional: job guards unrelated label additions from triggering a full re-scan
- [ ] Same treatment applied to qlty-new-file-gate.yml if applicable

## Context

- Related: t2065 (GH#18773) — original Qlty Smell Regression gate + `ratchet-bump` label override
- Related: t2068 — Qlty New-File Smell Gate with `new-file-smell-ok` label (same pattern)
- Observed regression: PR #19023 (GH#18787) — worker pushed 2 empty commits to get CI to re-evaluate after applying the label
- Cheap fix, highest-leverage because it eliminates a class of "worker churns commits" sessions

## Agent doc simplification (automated scan)

**File:** `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`
**Detected topic:** Unknown
**Current size:** 181 lines

### Classify before acting

**First, determine the file type** — the correct action depends on whether this is an instruction doc or a reference corpus:

- **Instruction doc** (agent rules, workflows, decision trees, operational procedures): Tighten prose, reorder by importance, split if multiple concerns. Follow guidance below.
- **Reference corpus** (SKILL.md, domain knowledge base, textbook-style content with self-contained sections): Do NOT compress content. Instead, split into chapter files with a slim index. See `tools/code-review/code-simplifier.md` "Reference corpora" classification (GH#6432).

### For instruction docs — proposed action

Tighten and restructure this agent doc. Follow `tools/build-agent/build-agent.md` guidance. Key principles:

1. **Preserve all institutional knowledge** — every verbose rule exists because something broke without it. Do not remove task IDs, incident references, error statistics, or decision rationale. Compress prose, not knowledge.
2. **Order by importance** — most critical instructions first (primacy effect: LLMs weight earlier context more heavily). Security rules, core workflow, then edge cases.
3. **Split if needed** — if the file covers multiple distinct concerns, extract sub-docs with a parent index. Use progressive disclosure (pointers, not inline content).
4. **Use search patterns, not line numbers** — any `file:line_number` references to other files go stale on every edit. Use `rg "pattern"` or section heading references instead.

### For reference corpora — proposed action

1. **Extract each major section** into its own file (e.g., `01-introduction.md`, `02-fundamentals.md`)
2. **Replace the original with a slim index** (~100-200 lines) — table of contents with one-line descriptions and file pointers
3. **Zero content loss** — every line moves to a chapter file, nothing is deleted or compressed
4. **Reconcile existing chapter files** — if partial splits already exist, deduplicate and keep the most complete version

### Verification

- Content preservation: all code blocks, URLs, task ID references (`tNNN`, `GH#NNN`), and command examples must be present before and after
- No broken internal links or references
- Agent behaviour unchanged (test with a representative query if possible)
- Qlty smells resolved for the target file: `~/.qlty/bin/qlty smells --all 2>&1 | grep '.agents/workflows/full-loop.md' | grep -c . | grep -q '^0$'` (report `SKIP` if Qlty is unavailable, not `FAIL`)

4. **Use search patterns, not line numbers** — any `file:line_number` references to other files go stale on every edit. Use `rg "pattern"` or section heading references instead.

### For reference corpora — proposed action

1. **Extract each major section** into its own file (e.g., `01-introduction.md`, `02-fundamentals.md`)
2. **Replace the original with a slim index** (~100-200 lines) — table of contents with one-line descriptions and file pointers
3. **Zero content loss** — every line moves to a chapter file, nothing is deleted or compressed
4. **Reconcile existing chapter files** — if partial splits already exist, deduplicate and keep the most complete version

### Verification

- Content preservation: all code blocks, URLs, task ID references (`tNNN`, `GH#NNN`), and command examples must be present before and after
- No broken internal links or references
- Agent behaviour unchanged (test with a representative query if possible)
- Qlty smells resolved for the target file: `~/.qlty/bin/qlty smells --all 2>&1 | grep '.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md' | grep -c . | grep -q '^0$'` (report `SKIP` if Qlty is unavailable, not `FAIL`)
- For reference corpora: `wc -l` total of chapter files >= original line count minus index overhead

### Confidence: medium

Automated scan flagged this file for maintainer review. The best simplification strategy requires human judgment — some files are appropriately structured already. Reference corpora (SKILL.md, domain knowledge bases) need restructuring into chapters, not content reduction.

title: t2108: fix(pulse-merge): make body keyword authoritative for linked issue extraction
body:
**Task ID:** `t2108` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~30m`
**Logged:** 2026-04-15
**Tags:** `bug` `pulse` `auto-dispatch` `interactive`

## Description

fix(pulse-merge): make body keyword authoritative for linked issue extraction — `_extract_linked_issue` in `pulse-merge.sh:967` falls back to matching `GH#NNN:` in PR titles even when the body has no closing keyword (`For #NNN`, `Ref #NNN`, planning-only PRs). The fallback then drives `_handle_post_merge_actions` to close the issue. t2099 (PR #19034) added a `parent-task` label guard at the close-call site; this fixes the leaf-issue half by making the title fallback only fire when the body ALSO has a closing keyword. Discovered live on 2026-04-15 — the t2105 brief PR (#19043) hit this exact pattern 14 minutes after the t2099 fix merged. 2-file change (function rewrite + new 4-scenario test), reference pattern is `tests/test-pulse-merge-parent-task-close-guard.sh`. **Implementation must use `tNNN:` title format, NOT `GH#NNN:`, to avoid the bug closing #19051 during its own fix's merge.**

## Task Brief

<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn -->

# t2108 — pulse-merge title fallback closes leaf issues despite `For #NNN`

**Issue:** GH#19051
**Tier:** `tier:simple` (Haiku)
**Origin:** interactive (Marcus, 2026-04-15, post-t2099 session)
**Estimate:** 30 min

## What

Make `_extract_linked_issue` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` body-keyword authoritative. The PR-title fallback (`GH#NNN: description`) must only return an issue number if the PR body **also** contains a closing keyword (`Closes`, `Closed`, `Fixes`, `Fixed`, `Resolves`, `Resolved`, case-insensitive, followed by `#NNN` referencing the same issue). The body keyword is the source of truth; the title is a tie-breaker for *which* of multiple body-matched issues is the primary one — never an override that creates a match where the body has none.

This is a regression closure — a 4-line behavioural change in a single function plus a 4-scenario test. The t2099 fix (parent-task label guard) covered parent issues; this fix covers the leaf-issue half of the same root cause.

## Why

Discovered live on 2026-04-15 across **three** consecutive sessions in a single evening:

| Session | PR | Issue closed prematurely | Recovery |
|---------|-----|--------------------------|----------|
| t2053.1 | #19028 (parent-task) | #18735 (parent roadmap) | Manual reopen + filed t2099 |
| t2099 | #19034 (the leaf-issue regression test wasn't enough) | — (covered) | — |
| t2105 planning | #19043 (planning-only brief PR) | #19042 (leaf bug) | Manual reopen + this brief |

The pattern: every PR in this repo follows the canonical title format `tNNN: description` or `GH#NNN: description` (per `.agents/AGENTS.md` "Git Workflow"). For PRs targeting an issue, the `GH#NNN:` form is dominant. `_extract_linked_issue` parses that title prefix as a fallback when the body has no closing keyword:

```bash
# pulse-merge.sh:984-991 (current behaviour)
# Match: GH#NNN prefix in PR title only (format: "GH#NNN: description").
issue_num=$(printf '%s' "$pr_title" | grep -oE 'GH#[0-9]+' | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+')
if [[ -n "$issue_num" ]]; then
    printf '%s' "$issue_num"
    return 0
fi
```

Then `_handle_post_merge_actions` calls `gh issue close "$linked_issue"` unconditionally (modulo the t2099 `parent-task` label guard). The body keyword check that the PR author *wanted* to honour is silently overridden by the title fallback.

The t2046 parent-task-keyword-guard prevents `Closes/Resolves/Fixes` from appearing in the PR body for parent-task issues. The t2099 label guard prevents the close call for parent-task issues at the merge end. Neither covers the case where:

1. The PR is a planning-only brief, multi-PR roadmap, or other "ship something against an issue without closing it"
2. The body intentionally uses `For #NNN` or `Ref #NNN` to avoid auto-close
3. The title still contains `GH#NNN:` because the title format is the canonical convention

That case currently breaks. The brief PR for t2105 (#19043) hit this exact pattern 14 minutes after t2099 (#19034) merged — same evening, same maintainer, same failure mode. The lesson is that the bug class is general, not parent-specific.

## How

### File 1: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` — make body keyword authoritative

Find the existing function `_extract_linked_issue` at **line 967**. The current body looks like (verbatim from line 967-994):

```bash
_extract_linked_issue() {
	local pr_number="$1"
	local repo_slug="$2"
	local pr_title pr_body
	pr_title=$(gh pr view "$pr_number" --repo "$repo_slug" --json title --jq '.title // empty' 2>/dev/null) || pr_title=""
	pr_body=$(gh pr view "$pr_number" --repo "$repo_slug" --json body --jq '.body // empty' 2>/dev/null) || pr_body=""

	# Match GitHub-native close keywords in the PR body only (case-insensitive).
	# Matches: close/closes/closed, fix/fixes/fixed, resolve/resolves/resolved.
	# Does NOT match bare GH#NNN, "Related #NNN", or other non-closing references. (GH#18098)
	local issue_num
	issue_num=$(printf '%s' "$pr_body" | grep -ioE '(close[ds]?|fix(es|ed)?|resolve[ds]?)\s+#[0-9]+' | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+')
	if [[ -n "$issue_num" ]]; then
		printf '%s' "$issue_num"
		return 0
	fi

	# Match: GH#NNN prefix in PR title only (format: "GH#NNN: description").
	# Title-scoped: bare GH#NNN references anywhere in the PR body are intentionally
	# excluded to avoid closing unrelated issues mentioned in "Related" sections. (GH#18098)
	issue_num=$(printf '%s' "$pr_title" | grep -oE 'GH#[0-9]+' | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+')
	if [[ -n "$issue_num" ]]; then
		printf '%s' "$issue_num"
		return 0
	fi

	return 0
}
```

**Replace the entire function body** with:

```bash
_extract_linked_issue() {
	local pr_number="$1"
	local repo_slug="$2"
	local pr_title pr_body
	pr_title=$(gh pr view "$pr_number" --repo "$repo_slug" --json title --jq '.title // empty' 2>/dev/null) || pr_title=""
	pr_body=$(gh pr view "$pr_number" --repo "$repo_slug" --json body --jq '.body // empty' 2>/dev/null) || pr_body=""

	# Match GitHub-native close keywords in the PR body only (case-insensitive).
	# Matches: close/closes/closed, fix/fixes/fixed, resolve/resolves/resolved.
	# Does NOT match bare GH#NNN, "Related #NNN", "For #NNN", "Ref #NNN", or other
	# non-closing references. (GH#18098 + t2108)
	#
	# The body keyword is AUTHORITATIVE. The title fallback below only fires when
	# the body has a closing keyword AND the title also names a number — it picks
	# WHICH issue from the body matches when there are multiple. It is NEVER an
	# override that creates a match where the body intentionally has none. (t2108)
	local body_issue title_issue
	body_issue=$(printf '%s' "$pr_body" | grep -ioE '(close[ds]?|fix(es|ed)?|resolve[ds]?)\s+#[0-9]+' | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+')
	title_issue=$(printf '%s' "$pr_title" | grep -oE 'GH#[0-9]+' | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+')

	# No closing keyword in the body → return empty. The PR is intentionally
	# not closing any issue (planning-only PR, multi-PR roadmap, "For #NNN"
	# reference, etc.). _handle_post_merge_actions will skip the close path
	# when this returns empty. (t2108)
	if [[ -z "$body_issue" ]]; then
		return 0
	fi

	# Body has a closing keyword. If the title also names a number, prefer the
	# title-named issue when it differs from body_issue (matches the historical
	# behaviour where the GH#NNN: title prefix is the primary identifier and
	# the body may reference additional issues). When they match or the title
	# has no number, return body_issue. (t2108)
	if [[ -n "$title_issue" ]]; then
		printf '%s' "$title_issue"
		return 0
	fi
	printf '%s' "$body_issue"
	return 0
}
```

The behavioural change in one sentence: **the body must contain a closing keyword for `_extract_linked_issue` to return any issue number.** If the body has no closing keyword, the function returns empty regardless of what's in the title, which causes `_handle_post_merge_actions` to skip the entire close path (the existing `if [[ -n "$linked_issue" ]]` guard handles this).

### File 2: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-extract-linked-issue.sh` — new test (4 scenarios)

Create a new test file that extracts `_extract_linked_issue` from `pulse-merge.sh` via `awk`/`eval` (same pattern as the existing `test-pulse-merge-parent-task-close-guard.sh` and `test-pulse-merge-rebase-nudge.sh`). Mock `gh pr view` to return canned title + body fixtures and assert the four scenarios below.

**Reference test pattern**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-parent-task-close-guard.sh` (created in t2099 / PR #19034). Copy its structure: setup_test_env / teardown_test_env / define_function_under_test / four assertions / main loop. The mock-gh stub there is directly applicable — just change which JSON keys it serves.

**Four scenarios (all must pass):**

| # | PR title | PR body | Expected return |
|---|----------|---------|-----------------|
| 1 | `GH#19042: plan t2105` | `For #19042\n\nNo closing keyword.` | empty (regression guard for the t2105 incident) |
| 2 | `GH#19042: fix bug` | `Resolves #19042\n` | `19042` (normal leaf close path still works) |
| 3 | `GH#19042: cross-issue` | `Closes #99999\n\nAlso references #19042.` | `19042` (title disambiguates when body has multiple closing keywords; matches historical behaviour) |
| 4 | `t2108: planning brief` | `Ref #19051\n` | empty (no GH#NNN in title AND no closing keyword in body — both gates fail) |

Scenario 1 is the regression guard. Scenarios 2 and 3 are existing-behaviour preservation. Scenario 4 covers the `tNNN:` title format that this very PR uses (and which doesn't trigger the title regex anyway).

### Verification

Run from the worktree, in this exact order:

```bash
# 1. ShellCheck the modified file
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh

# 2. Run the new test
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-extract-linked-issue.sh
# Expected: "Ran 4 tests, 0 failed."

# 3. Run the t2099 parent-task close guard test to confirm no regression there
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-parent-task-close-guard.sh
# Expected: "Ran 7 tests, 0 failed."

# 4. Sanity check: confirm _extract_linked_issue still extracts via awk/eval
awk '/^_extract_linked_issue\(\) \{/,/^}$/ { print }' .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh | grep -c "body_issue"
# Expected: at least 3 (declaration, assignment, conditional)
```

## Acceptance criteria

1. `_extract_linked_issue` returns empty when the PR body contains no closing keyword, regardless of the title (scenario 1).
2. `_extract_linked_issue` still returns the title-matched issue when the body has at least one closing keyword (scenarios 2, 3) — no regression on the existing leaf-issue close path.
3. New test file `tests/test-pulse-merge-extract-linked-issue.sh` exists, is executable, and all 4 assertions pass.
4. Existing `tests/test-pulse-merge-parent-task-close-guard.sh` still passes all 7 assertions (no regression in the t2099 parent-task path, which is independent and operates at the close-call layer).
5. `shellcheck` clean on `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` and the new test file.

## Out of scope

- **Removing the t2099 parent-task label guard.** It's defense in depth — even after this fix, a PR body with `Closes #parent-task-issue` would still try to close the parent if the keyword guard at PR creation time was bypassed. Both layers stay.
- **Changing PR title conventions.** The `GH#NNN:` title format is canonical and stays. This fix is about how `pulse-merge.sh` *interprets* that title, not about changing what authors write.
- **Refactoring `_handle_post_merge_actions`.** It already short-circuits on empty `linked_issue`; no changes needed there.
- **Updating documentation.** `prompts/build.txt` and `AGENTS.md` already say "the body keyword is the source of truth" implicitly — the fix makes the code match the existing intent.

## PR conventions

This PR closes a leaf bug, so the PR body MUST use `Resolves #19051`. **Use the `tNNN:` title format**, not `GH#NNN:`, to avoid the very bug being fixed during this fix's own merge:

```text
Title: t2108: fix(pulse-merge) make body keyword authoritative for linked issue extraction
Body:  Resolves #19051
```

(After this PR merges, future PRs targeting leaf issues can safely use `GH#NNN:` titles again.)

## Tier checklist (tier:simple)

- [x] ≤2 files modified (`pulse-merge.sh` + 1 new test file)
- [x] Verbatim code blocks for both files
- [x] No skeleton — every line is copy-pasteable
- [x] Test scenarios defined as a 4-row table with exact expected outputs
- [x] Estimate ≤1h (30 min)
- [x] 5 acceptance criteria (right at the limit; the 5th is a regression guard, not new behaviour)
- [x] No judgment keywords (no "consider", "decide", "evaluate")
- [x] Reference pattern explicitly named (`test-pulse-merge-parent-task-close-guard.sh` from t2099)

## Related

- **Root cause discovered in:** t2053.1 (PR #19028) → exposed parent-task case → fixed by t2099 (PR #19034)
- **Generalised in:** t2105 planning (PR #19043) → exposed leaf-issue case → this brief
- **Adjacent fix this complements:** t2099 / `_handle_post_merge_actions` parent-task label guard at line ~828 of `pulse-merge.sh`
- **PR title convention:** `.agents/AGENTS.md` Git Workflow section
- **Body keyword convention:** `.agents/templates/brief-template.md` "PR Conventions"
- **Related historical fix:** GH#18098 (the original fix that scoped title matching to `GH#NNN` only and excluded bare body references) — this PR is its second-order correction

title: t2109: fix(task-id-guard): read counter from origin/main tip instead of merge-base
body:
## What

Change `_find_merge_base()` + `_read_counter_at_ref()` in `.agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh` so the counter is read from the **tip of `origin/main`** (with a fallback chain), not from the merge-base between HEAD and origin/main. The merge-base lookup is what causes stale-worktree false positives.

## Why

The current `_check_message()` logic (`task-id-collision-guard.sh:207-275`):

1. Calls `_find_merge_base()` which returns `git merge-base HEAD origin/main`
2. Reads `.task-counter` from that merge-base ref
3. If a commit references `tNNN` where `NNN > counter`, flags it as invented

**Problem**: when a worktree is created *before* a subsequent `claim-task-id.sh` runs and pushes the counter bump, the merge-base is the pre-bump commit and its `.task-counter` value is stale. The guard blocks legitimate t-IDs that were claimed after worktree creation.

**Concrete repro (observed 2026-04-15 in session `a6ad2ada`):**

1. Worktree `chore/t2106-t2107-todo-entries` created at main tip X, `.task-counter` at X = 2106
2. `claim-task-id.sh --title "..."` pushed commit Y to `origin/main` → `.task-counter` = 2107
3. Second `claim-task-id.sh` pushed commit Z to `origin/main` → `.task-counter` = 2108
4. `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` invoked in the worktree with a commit subject referencing **t2106** and **t2107**
5. Guard ran `_find_merge_base` → returned X (from step 1, because worktree HEAD was still X)
6. `_read_counter_at_ref X` → 2106
7. t2107 numeric 2107 > counter 2106 → BLOCKED as "invented"

Both t-IDs were legitimately claimed; the remote counter was already 2108; the failure was purely because the worktree hadn't been rebased yet.

Workaround (manual, discovered during the session): `git stash -u && git rebase origin/main && git stash pop` — this moves HEAD forward to origin/main so merge-base returns the current tip. Works but is ceremony that should be the guard's problem, not the user's.

## How

Replace `_read_counter_at_ref "$merge_base"` with a counter resolution that takes the **maximum across multiple sources** — because `.task-counter` is monotonically increasing, the max is always the most-accurate known state:

```bash
# New helper — returns the max counter across known-good sources.
_resolve_current_counter() {
	local best=""
	local val ref
	# Priority sources, highest-freshness first. We take the MAX across all,
	# not the first — .task-counter is monotonic so max == most current.
	for ref in "origin/main" "origin/master" "main" "master" "HEAD"; do
		if git rev-parse --verify "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
			val=$(git show "${ref}:.task-counter" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')
			if [[ "$val" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
				if [[ -z "$best" || "$val" -gt "$best" ]]; then
					best="$val"
				fi
			fi
		fi
	done
	# Also consider working copy (covers detached-HEAD / no-remote edge cases)
	if [[ -f .task-counter ]]; then
		val=$(tr -d '[:space:]' < .task-counter)
		if [[ "$val" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
			if [[ -z "$best" || "$val" -gt "$best" ]]; then
				best="$val"
			fi
		fi
	fi
	[[ -n "$best" ]] && printf '%s' "$best"
	return 0
}
```

Then in `_check_message()` (around line 231):

```bash
local counter=""
counter=$(_resolve_current_counter)
if [[ -z "$counter" ]]; then
	_warn ".task-counter not readable from any source — fail-open"
	return 2
fi
```

The `merge_base` parameter becomes unused in `_check_message` — can be removed or kept for backwards compatibility (it's internal, removal is fine).

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh`
  - Add `_resolve_current_counter()` helper (~20 lines)
  - Replace the merge-base read in `_check_message()` with the resolver call
  - Optionally: remove `_find_merge_base()` since it becomes unused, or keep with a comment if something else references it
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-task-id-collision-guard.sh` — add regression test covering the stale-worktree scenario

### Test case to add (critical)

Setup:
1. Initialise a throwaway git repo with `.task-counter = 10` on `main`
2. Create a feature branch from main at counter=10
3. On main, increment `.task-counter` to 12 (simulates two more claims) and commit
4. Back on the feature branch, try to commit referencing `t11` and `t12`

Assertion: guard must allow the commit (returns 0) because `origin/main:.task-counter` at tip = 12, and both 11 and 12 are ≤ 12.

Also keep the existing test cases:

- Commit referencing `t2107` where counter=2106 and NO linked issue → still BLOCK (the genuine "invented" case)
- Commit referencing `t2107` where counter=2106 AND a `Resolves #19045` footer whose issue title starts with `t2107:` → still ALLOW (linked-issue fallback)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_resolve_current_counter()` function added to `.agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh`
- [ ] `_check_message()` uses the resolver, not merge-base
- [ ] New test case in `test-task-id-collision-guard.sh` for the stale-worktree scenario
- [ ] Existing tests still pass (regression guard)
- [ ] `shellcheck` clean on edited files
- [ ] Error message on legitimate violations unchanged (so operators still see the same format)

## Context

- **Observed**: session `a6ad2ada-97a3-4533-b74f-c70bb8eecb36`, 2026-04-15 01:42 UTC, during the filing of t2106 + t2107 (GH#19044 + GH#19045) TODO entries. Full detail in the session transcript.
- **Related**: t2047 — the original task-ID collision guard implementation. This issue refines it, does not revert.
- **Design note**: the guard is already fail-open in several places (gh unavailable, counter not readable). Adding the max-across-sources resolver is consistent with that philosophy — we'd rather miss a genuine violation than block legitimate work on a technicality. The `gh issue view` title cross-check at line 134 remains as the second line of defense.
- **Performance**: `git show` reads from the local object database without network access, so the multi-source resolution adds ~5 reads at commit time (~50ms). Negligible.

   - `--scan-all` — scan every `*.sh` under `.agents/scripts/` (used for the final zero-violation audit in Phase 6)
   - `--fix-hint` — print a remediation snippet per violation (pointing to shell-style-guide.md Pattern A or B)
   Exit codes: `0` clean, `1` violations found, `2` usage error.
2. **NEW:** `.github/workflows/shell-init-pattern-check.yml` — runs on `pull_request` against files matching `.agents/scripts/**/*.sh`. Invokes `shell-init-pattern-check.sh --scan-files` with only the diff (use `gh pr diff --name-only` or `git diff --name-only ${{ github.base_ref }}...HEAD`). Posts a PR comment with the violation list and a link to the style guide on failure.
3. **NEW:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-shell-init-pattern-check.sh` — regression test with positive and negative fixtures. Must cover: (a) plain unguarded `RED='...'` fails, (b) `readonly RED='...'` outside `shared-constants.sh` fails, (c) Pattern A (sourcing shared-constants) passes, (d) Pattern B (`[[ -z "${VAR+x}" ]] &&`) passes, (e) Pattern C (`TEST_RED=...`) passes, (f) unguarded `BOLD=` passes (not a canonical color per style guide §16-27), (g) the banned canonical set is RED/GREEN/YELLOW/BLUE/PURPLE/CYAN/WHITE/NC only.

## Why

Phase 1 landed the style guide but CI has no enforcement. Until the lint gate exists, new regressions can land undetected — which is exactly how GH#18702 happened in the first place. The gate is the structural fix: future PRs that introduce banned patterns fail CI at author time, not four days later when auto-update silently breaks.

This is also the pre-req that enables Phases 3–6. Those phases can physically land without Phase 2, but without the gate they can't be *verified*. The migration should be auto-checkable.

## How (worker guidance)

**Reference patterns:**
- Model the scanner CLI on `.agents/scripts/qlty-new-file-gate-helper.sh` (subcommand dispatch + diff-scoped scanning + PR comment posting).
- Model the workflow on `.github/workflows/qlty-new-file-gate.yml` (pull_request trigger, path filter, helper invocation, PR comment via `gh pr comment`).
- Model the test harness on `.agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-guard.sh` (tmpdir fixtures + positive/negative assertions + explicit pass/fail counter).
- Follow the shell style rules in the output you're enforcing: the helper itself MUST follow Pattern A (source `shared-constants.sh`) — it would be absurd for the enforcement script to violate its own rule.

**Detection logic:**
- Banned pattern 1: `^\s*(RED|GREEN|YELLOW|BLUE|PURPLE|CYAN|WHITE|NC)='` at top level (not inside a function body — check indentation/context or use `bashlisp`/`shfmt` AST as optional hardening; line-level regex is sufficient for v1).
- Banned pattern 2: `^\s*readonly\s+(RED|GREEN|YELLOW|BLUE|PURPLE|CYAN|WHITE|NC)=` anywhere outside `shared-constants.sh`.
- Safe: `[[ -z "${VAR+x}" ]]` guard on the same line or immediately before the assignment.
- Safe: any `RED|GREEN|...` assignment inside an `if`/function block (keep it simple for v1 — indentation > 0 = safe).
- `shared-constants.sh` is unconditionally exempt.

**Allowlisting for phased migration:** Phase 2 lands before Phases 3–6 complete, so there will still be ~18 production + ~12 test violations when this gate first runs. Two options (pick whichever is cleaner):
- (A) The gate runs only on PR-diffed files, so existing violations on main don't fail the workflow until someone touches them. Phases 3–6 then drain the known-violations list file-by-file.
- (B) Accept a temporary `.agents/configs/shell-init-pattern-allowlist.txt` listing the 18 production + 12 test files currently in violation. Phases 3–6 remove entries from the allowlist as each file migrates. Phase 6 deletes the allowlist entirely.

Option A is preferred — simpler, zero file churn, and aligns with how `qlty-new-file-gate.yml` handles the same problem. Choose B only if there's a specific reason to require zero-violation main from day one.

## Acceptance

1. `.agents/scripts/shell-init-pattern-check.sh` exists, is executable, shellcheck-clean.
2. `.github/workflows/shell-init-pattern-check.yml` exists and runs on PR.
3. `.agents/scripts/tests/test-shell-init-pattern-check.sh` exists and all assertions pass.
4. Helper correctly classifies every file listed in `.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md` §141-153 (the audit table).
5. A deliberately-planted violation fails CI on a demo PR (attach the failing run to the PR body).
6. The helper itself follows Pattern A.

- **Parent-task keyword rule:** use `For #18735` in the PR body. NEVER `Resolves`/`Closes`/`Fixes`. The parent stays open until Phase 7c merges.
- **Title format:** `t2053.2: shell init pattern lint gate (Phase 2)`

Add Pattern A near top.
5. **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/deploy-agents-on-merge.sh` (568 lines) — remove `GREEN/BLUE/YELLOW/RED/NC` at lines 30-34, add Pattern A.

These 5 helpers live in or adjacent to the `setup.sh` sourcing chain. `init-routines-helper.sh` (the GH#18702 fix) was one of this tier. [[ -f "${SCRIPT_DIR}/shared-constants.sh" ]] && source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/shared-constants.sh"

```bash

[[ -z "${BOLD+x}" ]] && BOLD='\033[1m'
```

title: t2053.7a: test harness Pattern C batch 1 (Phase 7a of t2053 roadmap)
body:
**Parent:** #18735 (t2053) — Phase 7a of 7. Test harness Pattern C normalization, batch 1 of 3.

**Parallelizable with:** Phases 7b and 7c (no file overlap).

## What

Migrate 5 test harnesses from `readonly RED='...'` etc. to Pattern C (prefixed names). **5 files, all edits.**

1. **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-circuit-breaker.sh` — lines 20-22 — rename `readonly RED/GREEN/YELLOW` → `readonly TEST_RED/TEST_GREEN/TEST_YELLOW`. Update all in-file references.
2. **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-command-logger.sh` — lines 19-21 — same rename + reference updates.
3. **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-matterbridge-helper.sh` — lines 19-21 — same.
4. **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh` — lines 10-11 — rename `readonly RED/GREEN` → `readonly TEST_RED/TEST_GREEN`.
5. **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-sandbox-sensitive-output-guard.sh` — lines 10-11 — same.

## Why

Per the style guide §72-85 (Pattern C), test harnesses should use prefixed color variables (`TEST_RED` etc.) to avoid any name collision with `shared-constants.sh`. These 5 test scripts currently use bare `readonly RED`, which is technically banned by the lint gate (§87-109) even though the private-scope safety net catches the issue at runtime.

Normalising them to Pattern C:
- Eliminates banned patterns from the scan (Phase 6 cleared production; these 3 phases clear tests).
- Enforces style consistency across the test corpus.
- Removes the last class of `readonly RED` declarations outside `shared-constants.sh`.

## How (worker guidance)

**Rename strategy per file:**

1. Rename the declaration:
   ```bash
   # BEFORE
   readonly RED='\033[0;31m'
   readonly GREEN='\033[0;32m'
   readonly YELLOW='\033[1;33m'

   # AFTER
   readonly TEST_RED='\033[0;31m'
   readonly TEST_GREEN='\033[0;32m'
   readonly TEST_YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
   ```

2. Update all references in the same file: `${RED}` → `${TEST_RED}`, `${GREEN}` → `${TEST_GREEN}`, `${YELLOW}` → `${TEST_YELLOW}`. Use a targeted `sed -i '' 's/\${RED}/${TEST_RED}/g'` (macOS syntax) or the Edit tool's `replaceAll`.

3. Run the test standalone to confirm: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-<name>.sh`. It should pass with the new variable names.

**Caveat:** if any of these test scripts *source* a production helper that depends on the bare `RED` name, the source will override the Pattern C names. Check with:
```bash
rg -n "source.*\.sh" <test-file>
```

If there's a `source`, confirm the production helper has been migrated to Pattern A (so it also uses shared-constants). After Phases 3-6, all production helpers do. The test then has both `RED` (from shared-constants) and `TEST_RED` (from itself) available — no conflict because Pattern C uses a different name.

**Reference:**
- Style guide §72-85 (Pattern C): `.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md`
- Prior art: any existing `TEST_*` usage in the test corpus (grep `rg "TEST_(RED|GREEN|YELLOW)"` for examples).

## Acceptance

1. All 5 test files use `TEST_*` prefixed names, not bare `RED/GREEN/YELLOW`.
2. All 5 test files pass when run standalone.
3. `shellcheck` clean on all 5 files.
4. If Phase 2 has landed: `shell-init-pattern-check.sh --scan-files` reports zero violations for these 5 files.
