# t2349 Brief — backfill-sub-issues: add umbrella-parent → children detection

**Issue:** GH#TBD (filed alongside this brief).

## Session origin

Discovered 2026-04-18 during board-clearing session after observing parent-tasks #19734 and #19736 had zero GitHub sub-issue links despite both bodies containing explicit `## Children` sections listing 7 and 4 children respectively. Manual `POST /repos/:owner/:repo/issues/:num/sub_issues` with child `id` (integer) linked all children cleanly. Root cause: the existing `backfill-sub-issues` path in `issue-sync-relationships.sh` runs CHILD-side only — `_backfill_one_issue` calls `_detect_parent_from_gh_state` on each candidate child and links upward when it finds one of three patterns (`tNNN.M` dot-notation title, `Parent:` line in body, `Blocked by:` referencing a parent-task-labeled issue). None of those patterns match the umbrella style where the PARENT carries the children list and the children never reference the parent. Result: a whole class of parent-tasks (decomposition umbrellas, retrospective trackers, roadmap epics) ship with a visible children table but no programmatic sub-issue graph, which then breaks `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh::_try_close_parent_tracker` (it falls back to a too-permissive body regex and mis-closes umbrellas on unrelated `#NNN` prose mentions — canonical: t2244/#19762 premature-close of #19734).

## What

Add parent-side detection to `backfill-sub-issues`: when iterating all issues, also check if the issue is a `parent-task` (by label) and, if so, parse its body for a `## Children` section and link every `#NNN` (or `GH#NNN`) reference in that section as a sub-issue.

## Why

- Umbrella-style parents never get their children linked programmatically — the only audit trail is prose in the body.
- `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh::_try_close_parent_tracker` (t2244/#19762 target) needs the authoritative sub-issue graph to avoid false closures. Without umbrella-side detection, it will keep falling back to body regex.
- GitHub UI shows sub-issue progress in the sidebar; unlinked children look like orphans.
- Framework principle: the harness should wire relationships at creation/sync time, not require an agent to remember to POST manually.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-relationships.sh:619-665` — extend `_backfill_one_issue` OR add a sibling `_backfill_parent_children($parent_num, $repo)` that runs when the issue carries the `parent-task` label.
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-relationships.sh:676-730` — in `cmd_backfill_sub_issues`, fetch labels alongside title/body and dispatch to child-side or parent-side logic.
- **EXTEND** test: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-backfill-sub-issues.sh` — add cases for umbrella-style parent with `## Children` section listing 4 children. Mirror the existing Class B test harness.
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh:1497-1503` — update docstring to document the new parent-side detection pattern.

### Reference pattern

The child-side detection at `issue-sync-relationships.sh:619` shows the exact shape to mirror — fetch title+body, detect pattern, resolve node IDs via `_cached_node_id`, call `_gh_add_sub_issue`. The new function should:
1. Accept parent issue number + repo.
2. Fetch parent body (already fetched in the outer loop — pass it in to avoid double-fetch).
3. Parse the body for a `## Children` heading (case-insensitive, allow `## Child Issues`, `## Sub-issues`, `## Phases` as aliases).
4. In that section, extract every `#NNN` / `GH#NNN` reference (anchored to line start with `-` list marker to avoid prose matches).
5. For each extracted number, resolve its node ID and call `_gh_add_sub_issue($parent_node, $child_node)`.
6. Return count of links made (for summary output).

### Extraction regex candidate

```bash
rg -oE '^[[:space:]]*-[^-]*#([0-9]+)' | sed -E 's/.*#([0-9]+).*/\1/'
```

Validate against both umbrella styles observed today:

- `#19734` body: `| HIGH | t2229 | #19735 | ...` (markdown table)
- `#19736` body: `- t2229 / #19738 — CI workflow cascade-vulnerability linter` (markdown list)

Table-cell regex needs to tolerate both.

### Self-healing hook

Run parent-side backfill from the existing pulse reconcile phase `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:1236` (already wired to call `backfill-sub-issues`). No new scheduling needed — the addition just widens what the periodic pass detects.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `issue-sync-helper.sh backfill-sub-issues --issue 19734 --dry-run` reports 7 children that would be linked (all of #19735, #19737, #19743, #19744, #19751, #19752, #19753).
2. Without `--dry-run`, the same command produces `sub_issues_summary.total = 7` on #19734.
3. Idempotent — running twice doesn't error or duplicate.
4. Existing child-side detection still works for the three legacy patterns (dot-notation, `Parent:` line, `Blocked by:` with parent-task label). No regression on `test-backfill-sub-issues.sh` Class A + Class B cases.
5. New test case: fixture umbrella issue body with `## Children` section + 3 children issues; assert all 3 get linked.
6. Prose body text like "see #19678" or "resolved by PR #19680" OUTSIDE the `## Children` section does NOT produce a false link.
7. Verification command: `gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/19734/sub_issues" --jq '[.[] | .number] | sort'` returns the child list.

## Tier

**tier:standard** — single-file change in existing helper, extends well-tested pattern, has clear acceptance criteria and verification command. Not tier:simple because the section-parsing and regex choice are judgment calls that benefit from Sonnet review.

## Related

- GH#19762 / t2244 (parent) — the `_try_close_parent_tracker` bug that misfires when the sub-issue graph is empty; this task addresses the upstream "graph is empty" root cause by populating it.
- GH#19093 / t2114 — original backfill-sub-issues feature (child-side detection); this task is the Phase 2 extension.
- Canonical parents needing this fix: #19734 (v3.8.71 retrospective, 7 children), #19736 (harness self-inflicted CI failure class, 4 children). Already wired manually during the filing session — test by running backfill and confirming idempotence.

# t2350 Brief — pulse: auto-rebase or auto-close DIRTY PRs

**Issue:** GH#TBD (filed alongside this brief).

## Session origin

Discovered 2026-04-18 during board-clearing session. Three `origin:interactive` PRs (#19754, #19703, #19696) had accumulated merge conflicts with main (`mergeStateStatus: DIRTY`) and sat unmerged for 1-2 days. Each required interactive rebase + triage decision (#19754 and #19703 closed as superseded; #19696 rebased and merged). The pulse has no periodic sweep for DIRTY PRs, so stuck PRs accumulate until an interactive session clears them.

## What

Add a pulse-stage scanner that detects DIRTY PRs and takes one of two actions based on age and content:

- **Auto-rebase**: if PR is <48h old AND has real code changes AND only TODO.md is conflicting → rebase onto `origin/main`, resolve TODO.md by accepting HEAD + re-inserting the PR's task entry at correct chronological position, force-push.
- **Auto-close**: if PR is >7d old AND hasn't had a human push in 3d → close with a comment explaining "superseded by subsequent merges" and link to any issue that remains open for worker re-dispatch.

## Why

- Interactive users file planning PRs (TODO.md + brief file) that go DIRTY within hours of any other TODO.md push.
- Workers that complete work but get delayed through review bot gate age into DIRTY.
- Nobody schedules manual DIRTY-PR triage, so stuck PRs pile up until a session notices them.
- Both actions (rebase if possible, close if stale) are deterministic and idempotent — no human judgment needed in the common case.

## How

**NEW: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh`** — new pulse stage.

**EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`** — register the new stage after the merge pass.

**Reference pattern**: model on `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` (pulse stage lifecycle: state file, dedup lock, gh query loop, comment on action).

### Detection

```bash
gh pr list --state open --json number,mergeStateStatus,updatedAt,author,labels,files \
  --jq '.[] | select(.mergeStateStatus == "DIRTY")'
```

### Auto-rebase path

Eligibility: all true:
- `mergeStateStatus == "DIRTY"`
- PR age < 48h
- `author.login == OWNER || labels contains "origin:worker"`
- Conflicting files list (from `git merge-tree --write-tree`) includes ONLY TODO.md
- Branch still exists on origin

Action:
1. Create ephemeral worktree for the PR branch.
2. Attempt `git rebase origin/main`. If ONLY TODO.md conflicts, resolve via `git checkout --ours TODO.md` + re-insert the PR's task entry (extracted via `git show $commit -- TODO.md`) at correct chronological position.
3. `git push --force-with-lease origin <branch>`.
4. Remove ephemeral worktree.
5. Post PR comment documenting the rebase.

### Auto-close path

Eligibility: all true:
- `mergeStateStatus == "DIRTY"`
- PR age > 7d
- No human commits in last 3d (check `commits[-1].author.login` against repo maintainer list)
- No `do-not-close` label

Action:
1. Post PR comment explaining closure (template with issue back-link if applicable).
2. `gh pr close --delete-branch`.

### Safety gates

- Dry-run mode (`DRY_RUN=1` env var) prints would-be actions without executing.
- Never rebases a PR with non-TODO.md conflicts — escalate to a maintainer-review comment instead.
- Never auto-closes a PR with `do-not-close` label OR linked to an OPEN issue with `parent-task` label.
- Audit log: every action written to `audit-log-helper.sh log dirty-pr-sweep`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh --dry-run` against current repo lists 0 or more DIRTY PRs with the proposed action (rebase / close / escalate).
2. Test harness `tests/test-dirty-pr-sweep.sh` with fixtures for all three paths.
3. Registered in `pulse-wrapper.sh` to run every Nth pulse cycle (every 30min is fine — not per-cycle).
4. Idempotent — re-running within 30min doesn't re-action the same PR.
5. Never rebases `parent-task` PRs (those have their own rules).
6. Verification: open a fixture DIRTY PR, run the sweep, confirm rebase succeeds OR close fires per eligibility.

## Tier

`tier:thinking` — architectural decisions (which pulse stage, what eligibility windows, rebase conflict resolution heuristics) benefit from deeper reasoning. NOT `tier:simple` — many judgment calls.

## Related

- PR #19696 (rebased manually during this session) — canonical eligible-for-auto-rebase case.
- PRs #19754, #19703 (closed manually during this session) — canonical eligible-for-auto-close case.

# t2351 Brief — pulse: periodic canonical-repo fast-forward + stale worktree cleanup

**Issue:** GH#TBD (filed alongside this brief).

## Session origin

Discovered 2026-04-18 during board-clearing session: (a) canonical `~/Git/aidevops` was 2 commits behind `origin/main` at session start — no harness keeps it current; (b) `git worktree list` reported 169 total worktrees, with ~30 dating from 2026-04-15 (3 days stale) whose branches were already merged. The existing `worktree-helper.sh clean --auto --force-merged` handles the cleanup but isn't scheduled, and nothing keeps canonical main fresh for interactive sessions that land on it by default.

## What

Add two scheduled maintenance tasks to the pulse:

1. **Canonical-repo fast-forward**: for every repo in `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json`, run `git fetch origin && git checkout main && git pull --ff-only origin main` if the working tree is clean and no active session is mid-edit.
2. **Stale worktree sweep**: for every repo, invoke `worktree-helper.sh clean --auto --force-merged` to drop worktrees whose branch is merged or PR is closed.

Both run on a cadence (every ~30min is sufficient — not per-cycle).

## Why

- Interactive sessions start on canonical main by default. Stale main causes false `pre-edit-check.sh` decisions and requires manual `git pull`.
- Stale worktrees consume disk, clutter `git worktree list`, and confuse the cross-session ownership check (`pre-edit-check.sh` "ownership conflict" logic).
- Both operations are deterministic and safe with the right gates (fail-open on uncommitted changes, respect active-session stamps).
- Agent doesn't need to remember to run these — the harness should.

## How

**NEW**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh` — new pulse stage combining both operations.

**EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — register after existing merge/dispatch passes (runs once every ~30min via cadence counter).

**Reference pattern**: follow `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification.sh` lifecycle (state file, cadence gate, per-repo loop, audit log).

### Fast-forward logic

For each repo in `repos.json` where `pulse: true`:

1. Skip if repo is `local_only: true`.
2. `git -C $repo status --porcelain` — skip if any output (dirty tree).
3. `git -C $repo stash list` — skip if stash non-empty (session in-flight).
4. Check `.agents/active-session-stamps/` or equivalent — skip if active session owns canonical.
5. `git -C $repo fetch origin --prune --quiet`.
6. Check `git -C $repo rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main`. If 0, done. Otherwise:
7. `git -C $repo checkout main && git -C $repo pull --ff-only origin main`.
8. Log result via `audit-log-helper.sh log canonical-maintenance`.

### Worktree cleanup logic

For each repo in `repos.json`:

1. Skip if `local_only: true`.
2. `worktree-helper.sh clean --auto --force-merged` — the existing helper handles eligibility (merged branches, closed PRs via `gh pr list`, squash-merge detection).
3. Log summary via audit log.

### Timeout + safety

- Hard timeout per repo (60s each) — the worktree cleanup was observed to spawn 13 runaway processes during manual run (2026-04-18); add `timeout 60 worktree-helper.sh ...` or equivalent and track why it was slow (likely per-worktree `gh pr list` network round-trips).
- Before scheduling, investigate why `worktree-helper.sh clean --auto --force-merged` ran >3min on a 166-worktree checkout — may be a linear scan without batching. File as follow-up if so.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh --dry-run` lists repos needing fast-forward and stale worktrees without mutating state.
2. Real run fast-forwards canonical main for every clean repo and removes every merged worktree.
3. Dirty tree → skip (no stash, no reset).
4. Active session stamp → skip (no clobber).
5. Audit log entries for every action.
6. Test harness `tests/test-pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh` covers skip-on-dirty, skip-on-session-active, successful fast-forward, worktree cleanup integration.
7. Registered in `pulse-wrapper.sh` on a 30min cadence — not per-cycle.
8. Per-repo hard timeout prevents runaway (60s per repo is a generous default).

## Tier

`tier:standard` — well-defined mechanics, one new pulse stage, clear safety gates.

## Related

- Existing `worktree-helper.sh clean --auto --force-merged` handles the cleanup mechanics — this task only schedules and gates it.
- `pulse-simplification.sh` is the cadence-gated template to copy.
- Canonical repo was 2 commits behind origin at 2026-04-18 21:30 UTC — caught manually during board-clearing session.

title: bug(stats): stats-wrapper.sh missing AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=true — regression of GH#18670 blocks quality-debt dispatch
body:
## Description

`stats-wrapper.sh` runs the review-feedback scanner under launchd/systemd/cron with no TTY but without setting any headless signal. `detect_session_origin()` therefore defaults to `interactive`, so every `quality-debt` issue it creates is tagged `origin:interactive` AND auto-assigned to the runner. The pulse's GH#18352 dedup guard then treats the combination as an active interactive claim and permanently blocks dispatch.

This is a direct regression of GH#18670. PR #18676 added `export AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=true` to `pulse-wrapper.sh` main() but did not extend the fix to `stats-wrapper.sh`, which runs the same `gh_create_issue` code path through a separate scheduler.

Contradicts the documented intent at `.agents/scripts/quality-feedback-issues-lib.sh:315-319`:

> Keep the issue unassigned and explicitly dispatchable. The worker claim adds the real assignee at launch time; pre-assigning the repo owner here collapses backlog ownership and execution claim into the same field, which makes the pulse skip fresh quality-debt work.

## Expected Behavior

Quality-debt issues created by the 15-min stats sweep should be unassigned and tagged `origin:worker` — immediately dispatchable by the pulse.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Boot a machine with `aidevops-stats-wrapper.service` enabled (or launchd equivalent on macOS) and at least one merged PR with review-bot feedback within the scan window.
2. Wait for the 15-minute stats tick to fire `stats-wrapper.sh`.
3. Observe the newly-created `quality-debt` issues carry `origin:interactive` and are self-assigned to the runner.
4. Observe the pulse's next dispatch cycle skipping them with `Dedup: #N in SLUG already assigned — ASSIGNED: ... to RUNNER`.

## Root Cause

**File:** `.agents/scripts/stats-wrapper.sh`
**Function:** `main()` (line 150)

Call chain:

```text
aidevops-stats-wrapper.timer (15m)
  -> stats-wrapper.sh main()
    -> run_daily_quality_sweep      (stats-functions.sh)
      -> _sweep_review_scanner      (stats-quality-sweep.sh)
        -> quality-feedback-helper.sh scan-merged --create-issues
          -> _create_new_quality_debt_issue   (quality-feedback-issues-lib.sh:373)
            -> gh_create_issue       (shared-constants.sh:1019)
              |-- session_origin_label() -> "origin:interactive"    (the bug)
              `-- _gh_wrapper_auto_assignee -> RUNNER               (t2028 auto-assign)
```

`detect_session_origin()` at `shared-constants.sh:834` returns `worker` only when one of `AIDEVOPS_SESSION_ORIGIN`, `FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS`, `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS`, `OPENCODE_HEADLESS`, or `GITHUB_ACTIONS` is set. Under the timer none are set, so it falls through to the `interactive` default.

`pulse-wrapper.sh:1361-1369` sets `export AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=true` at the top of `main()` precisely to avoid this. `stats-wrapper.sh main()` has no equivalent.

## Direct Evidence (local install, 2026-04-19)

Five stuck `quality-debt` issues on a managed private repo, all created in one `stats-wrapper.sh` run at 14:52-14:55 UTC covering 5 distinct files across 5 merged PRs.

`~/.aidevops/logs/stats.log`:

```text
[stats-wrapper] Starting at 2026-04-19T14:52:07Z
  Created issue #N1: quality-debt: <file-1> — PR #P1 review feedback (medium)
  Created issue #N2: quality-debt: <file-2> — PR #P2 review feedback (medium)
  Created issue #N3: quality-debt: <file-3> — PR #P3 review feedback (high)
  Created issue #N4: quality-debt: <file-4> — PR #P4 review feedback (medium)
  Created issue #N5: quality-debt: <file-5> — PR #P5 review feedback (medium)
[stats-wrapper] Finished at 2026-04-19T14:55:55Z
```

`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` (next dispatch cycle):

```text
[pulse-wrapper] Dedup: #N3 in <managed-private-repo> already assigned — ASSIGNED: issue #N3 in <managed-private-repo> is assigned to <RUNNER>
[dispatch_with_dedup] Dedup guard blocked #N3 in <managed-private-repo>
```

Labels confirmed via REST before the hotfix:

```json
{"assignees":["<RUNNER>"],"number":N3,
 "labels":["status:available","quality-debt","source:review-feedback",
           "priority:high","origin:interactive"]}
```

## Fix

Mirror the `pulse-wrapper.sh:1369` pattern at the top of `stats-wrapper.sh main()`:

```bash
main() {
    # GH#<this-issue>: declare this process as headless BEFORE anything
    # else runs so every child shell (quality-feedback-helper.sh ->
    # _create_new_quality_debt_issue -> gh_create_issue ->
    # session_origin_label) returns "worker". Mirrors pulse-wrapper.sh:1369
    # and closes the GH#18670 regression in the stats scheduler.
    export AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=true

    # ... existing --self-check / --dry-run / dedup / main logic ...
```

Scope: one line added, comment block explaining rationale. No behaviour change for existing users except that new `quality-debt` issues will be `origin:worker` + unassigned, as documented in `quality-feedback-issues-lib.sh:315-319`.

## Cross-Platform Scope (NOT Linux-specific)

`setup-modules/schedulers.sh::setup_stats_wrapper()` generates both a macOS launchd plist (lines 955-996) and a Linux systemd/cron unit (lines 1003-1014). **Neither sets `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=true` as an environment variable**, so macOS users are affected identically to Linux users. The fix in the script is runtime-agnostic — no scheduler-template change needed.

## Secondary (informational — not part of this fix)

The audit that surfaced this also flagged `shellcheck-wrapper.sh` as "missing `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS`". That's a false positive — `shellcheck-wrapper.sh` wraps the `shellcheck` binary with RSS watchdog and rate limiting. It never calls `gh` or `gh_create_issue`, so it does not need the headless declaration. Worth documenting as "wrappers that run `gh_create_issue` need this; shell-out wrappers do not."

## Suggested Verification

1. Add `export AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=true` to `stats-wrapper.sh` `main()`.
2. Regression test (mirror the existing `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-headless-export.sh`): assert that a subshell invocation of `stats-wrapper.sh` main observes `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=true` before `run_daily_quality_sweep` is called, and that `detect_session_origin` returns `worker` inside the stats run.
3. Optional: sweep the repo for other `*-wrapper.sh` entrypoints that call `gh_create_issue` / `gh_create_pr` (directly or through `quality-feedback-helper.sh`, `issue-sync-helper.sh`, etc.) and lack the export.

## Local Hotfix Applied

While waiting for the upstream fix:

1. Added `export AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=true` to the DEPLOYED `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/stats-wrapper.sh` `main()` (will be overwritten at next `aidevops update`, by which time the upstream fix should land).
2. Verified via `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=true bash -c 'source shared-constants.sh; detect_session_origin'` → `worker`.
3. `stats-wrapper.sh --self-check` → PASS.
4. Unstuck the 5 blocked issues on the affected private repo via REST: swapped `origin:interactive` → `origin:worker`, removed the runner as assignee. Verified all 5 now read `{"assignees":[],"origin_labels":["origin:worker"]}`.

## Environment

- aidevops version: 3.8.74 (latest: 3.8.75)
- AI Assistant: OpenCode
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Shell: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- gh CLI: gh version 2.90.0 (2026-04-16)

## Additional Context

- Prior fix: GH#18670 closed 2026-04-13 via PR #18676 (merged 17:49:48Z).
- PR #18676 files: `pulse-wrapper.sh`, `pulse-triage.sh`, `post-merge-review-scanner.sh`, `cleanup-mistagged-origin-interactive.sh`, `tests/test-pulse-wrapper-headless-export.sh` — did not include `stats-wrapper.sh`.
- Dedup rule being triggered: `AGENTS.md` "General dedup rule — combined signal (t1996)" + `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh is-assigned` Layer 6 interactive-session protection (GH#18352).

title: t2387: route no_work crashes to skip tier escalation
body:
When worker-watchdog reports crash_type=no_work (worker exited during infra setup without reading brief), escalate_issue_tier currently still cascades tier:simple -> tier:standard -> tier:thinking. This wastes progressively more expensive models on the same infrastructure failure. The t2119 guard already skips the body-quality gate for no_work, but the tier escalation itself still fires. Fix: when crash_type=no_work, skip tier escalation entirely and keep the issue at its original tier. Rely on existing circuit breakers (cost-circuit-breaker, stale-recovery, dispatch-dedup-stale) to apply NMR if retries fail repeatedly. These apply markers that t2386 already recognizes as breaker trips so NMR is preserved correctly. Files: .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh escalate_issue_tier (line 825-1014). Current evidence: issues #19733, #19738, #19749 have 5 dispatches / 0 kills (workers exit cleanly without PR, likely no_work crashes) — at current tier:simple they are now at tier:thinking after escalation.

title: t2389: tier:simple body-shape validator (auto-downgrade mis-tiered briefs pre-dispatch)
body:
# t2389: tier:simple body-shape validator (auto-downgrade mis-tiered briefs pre-dispatch)

**Session origin:** interactive
**Severity:** high — every mis-tiered dispatch burns the full haiku→sonnet→opus cascade
**Tier:** standard

## What

Add a pre-dispatch validator that inspects the body shape of any `tier:simple`-labelled issue and auto-downgrades to `tier:standard` when the body contains hard disqualifiers documented in `reference/task-taxonomy.md` "Tier Assignment Validation". The validator:

1. Runs **after** `_ensure_issue_body_has_brief` and **before** `_run_predispatch_validator` in `pulse-dispatch-core.sh::dispatch_with_dedup`
2. Only activates for issues carrying `tier:simple`
3. Parses the body for 4 high-precision disqualifiers (see "How")
4. On disqualifier hit: swaps `tier:simple` → `tier:standard`, posts a feedback comment citing the specific disqualifier, returns 0 (dispatch proceeds at `tier:standard`)
5. On no hit: returns 0 (dispatch proceeds at `tier:simple`)
6. Non-blocking: never returns non-zero, never closes the issue

## Why

Issues are routinely mis-tagged `tier:simple` at creation time despite failing multiple disqualifiers. Once dispatched, haiku fails (judgment work it can't do), the pulse escalates to sonnet (12x cost), sonnet fails or succeeds after extensive exploration, and the cascade report gets filed. This wastes 1-2 dispatch cycles per mis-tier.

The taxonomy doc already has a "Quick-Check at Creation Time" list but it's only enforced by human discipline at `/new-task` time. Server-side enforcement at dispatch is defence-in-depth — it catches issues that were tagged before the rules existed, issues whose tier label was overridden later, and issues where the task-creator skipped the checklist.

Evidence: the broader 17-issue audit that produced this task identified at least 3 issues mis-tagged `tier:simple` when they required architectural reasoning. The issue-level damage is low per occurrence but recurrent.

## How

### Files to modify

- **NEW:** `.agents/scripts/tier-simple-body-shape-helper.sh` — the validator helper. Model on `.agents/scripts/pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh` for structure, but simpler (no generator marker parsing, no scratch clone — pure body-string inspection).
- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh` (around line 952-959, between `_ensure_issue_body_has_brief` and `_run_predispatch_validator`) — add one call to the new helper.
- **NEW:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tier-simple-body-shape.sh` — fixture-based tests.
- **EDIT:** `.agents/reference/task-taxonomy.md` — add a "Server-side enforcement" subsection under "Tier Assignment Validation" citing the new helper.
- **EDIT:** `.agents/AGENTS.md` — add a one-liner in the "Briefs, Tiers, and Dispatchability" section pointing at the validator.

### Disqualifier checks (MVP set — 4 of 9 from taxonomy)

High-precision only. The other 5 (skeleton code, conditional logic, error handling, cross-package, large-file + no verbatim) require fuzzier heuristics and are deferred.

1. **File count >2** — parse `## Files to modify` / `## Files to Modify` / `## How` sections; count lines matching `^[\s-]*(NEW:|EDIT:)` or bullet points containing explicit file paths (`\.(sh|py|md|ts|tsx|js|jsx|yml|yaml|json|toml|go|rs)`). Exit 10 if count > 2.
2. **Estimate >1h** — parse `~Nh`, `~Nm`, or `~Nd` tokens. Convert to minutes. Exit 10 if > 60 minutes.
3. **Acceptance criteria >4** — count `- [ ]` checkboxes inside a `## Acceptance` or `## Acceptance Criteria` section. Exit 10 if count > 4.
4. **Judgment keywords present** — case-insensitive grep for the token set: `graceful degradation`, `fallback`, `retry`, `conditional`, `coordinate`, `design`, `architecture`, `trade-off`, `strategy`. Exit 10 if any hit.

Each disqualifier is a separate `_check_*` function returning 0=pass, 10=fail with a populated `$DISQUALIFIER_REASON` global.

### Integration hook

In `pulse-dispatch-core.sh::dispatch_with_dedup` just after `_ensure_issue_body_has_brief`:

```bash
_run_tier_simple_body_shape_check "$issue_number" "$repo_slug"
# Non-blocking — always returns 0 so dispatch proceeds. If a disqualifier
# was detected the helper already mutated the labels and posted feedback.
```

The helper is a separate script (not sourced) to keep dispatch-core.sh blast radius small.

### Feedback comment format

Idempotent via `<!-- tier-simple-auto-downgrade -->` marker. Body:

```markdown
<!-- tier-simple-auto-downgrade -->
## Tier Auto-Downgrade: simple → standard

Pre-dispatch body-shape check detected a `tier:simple` disqualifier. Swapping `tier:simple` → `tier:standard` before worker dispatch.

**Disqualifier:** <specific reason>

**Evidence:** <quoted body fragment>

The worker is still dispatching — just at the appropriate tier. See `.agents/reference/task-taxonomy.md` "Tier Assignment Validation" for the full disqualifier list.

_Automated by `tier-simple-body-shape-helper.sh` (t2389)._
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `tier-simple-body-shape-helper.sh` exists and is shellcheck-clean
- [ ] 4 `_check_*` functions implemented with clear return conventions
- [ ] `_apply_downgrade` helper that swaps labels + posts comment (idempotent via marker)
- [ ] `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` wires in the new check between freshness guard and pre-dispatch validator
- [ ] `test-tier-simple-body-shape.sh` covers each disqualifier with a pass + fail fixture
- [ ] Clean dispatch (no `tier:simple` label) is a no-op
- [ ] Idempotency test: running twice on same issue does not post duplicate comment

## Context

Related to the broader pipeline-autonomy investigation. Companion fixes:
- t2386 (#19909, merged) — NMR circuit-breaker loop
- t2387 (#19918, merged) — no_work crash tier-escalation skip
- t2388 (#19928, open) — parent-task decomposition nudge

This is Fix #6 of that investigation. Fix #4 (duplicate close) and Fix #5 (age-based closure) are done/deferred respectively.

## Tier checklist (this brief)

- [x] Files to modify: 5 (helper, dispatch-core, test, taxonomy doc, AGENTS.md) — above tier:simple threshold of 2
- [x] Estimate: ~2h — above tier:simple threshold of 1h
- [x] Acceptance criteria: 7 — above tier:simple threshold of 4
- [x] Judgment keywords in How section: "coordinate" (for label/comment mutations), "design" (of the disqualifier detection heuristics)

All four hard disqualifiers hit → `tier:standard` is correct. This brief is, somewhat fittingly, exactly the kind of brief the validator it proposes would reject as tier:simple.

title: pulse-prefetch: delta fetch always falls back to full sweep due to ${2:-{}} bash expansion bug
body:
## Description

`_prefetch_repo_prs` and `_prefetch_repo_issues` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch.sh` both start with:

```bash
local cache_entry="${2:-{}}"
```

Bash parses `${PARAM:-WORD}` by terminating `WORD` at the first unescaped `}`, so this expands to "default is `{`" followed by a literal `}`. When `$2` is empty (new-cache path) the result happens to equal `{}`. When `$2` is a non-empty JSON string (the normal delta path, where the caller passes the cached entry from `_prefetch_cache_get`), the local variable becomes the original value plus a trailing `}` — invalid JSON.

Every downstream `jq` call on `cache_entry` then fails. The `.last_prefetch` lookup in `_prefetch_prs_try_delta` / `_prefetch_issues_try_delta` returns empty, the `[[ -z "$last_prefetch" ]]` guard fires, and the helper logs:

```text
[pulse-wrapper] _prefetch_repo_{prs,issues}: delta fetch failed for <owner>/<repo>
  (falling back to full): no timestamp or fetch error
```

Net effect: delta has **never** produced a success since this line was written. Every cycle runs a full `gh pr list --json …` and `gh issue list --json …` instead of the cheap `updated:>=<ts>` search GH#15286 introduced.

## Expected Behaviour

On the second and subsequent pulse cycles (after the first full sweep seeds `last_prefetch` in the cache), `_prefetch_repo_prs` / `_prefetch_repo_issues` should take the delta path and emit log lines like:

```text
[pulse-wrapper] _prefetch_repo_{prs,issues}: delta for <owner>/<repo>: N changed (PRs|issues) merged into cache
```

consuming a fraction of the GraphQL points that a full sweep uses.

## Steps to Reproduce

Direct bash reproducer (no pulse needed):

```bash
f() {
  local x="${2:-{}}"
  printf 'in=%q (len=%d) out=%q (len=%d)\n' "$2" "${#2}" "$x" "${#x}"
}
f slug ''
f slug '{}'
f slug '{"a":1}'
f slug '{"last_prefetch":"2026-04-19T10:00:00Z"}'
```

Output (reproduced on bash 5.2.21):

```text
in=''                                             (len=0)  out=\{\}                                              (len=2)
in=\{\}                                           (len=2)  out=\{\}\}                                            (len=3)
in=\{\"a\":1\}                                    (len=7)  out=\{\"a\":1\}\}                                     (len=8)
in=\{\"last_prefetch\":\"2026-04-19T10:00:00Z\"\} (len=39) out=\{\"last_prefetch\":\"2026-04-19T10:00:00Z\"\}\}  (len=41)
```

The extra trailing `}` is the bug.

End-to-end reproducer (full pipeline, requires a populated `pulse-prefetch-cache.json`):

1. Corrupt the `state_fingerprint` field in the cache for a repo so the cache-hit short-circuit misses.
2. Source `pulse-prefetch.sh` and call `_prefetch_repo_prs <slug> "$(jq -c '.["<owner>/<repo>"]' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-prefetch-cache.json)"`.
3. Observe `cache_entry` arriving at `_prefetch_prs_try_delta` with length = original + 1, `jq -r '.last_prefetch // ""'` returning empty, and the `"no timestamp or fetch error"` log line firing.

## Evidence from a live pulse log

- Total log lines: 220,825
- `"delta fetch failed for"` occurrences: **1,928**
- Delta-success log line (`"delta for .+: [0-9]+ changed (PRs|issues) merged into cache"`): **0**
- `STATE CACHE HIT` (fingerprint-based short-circuit that bypasses the buggy wrappers): 1,205 — these cycles succeed, which is why the cache stays warm and the bug only manifests as wasted quota rather than broken state.
- First failure: log line 98,314 (shortly after `pulse-prefetch.sh` landed).
- Most recent failure: log line 220,477 (current).

## Root cause

Bash parameter expansion grammar: `${PARAM:-WORD}` terminates `WORD` at the first unescaped `}`. Inside the double-quoted string `"${2:-{}}"`, the parser reads `${2:-{}` as the expansion (default = `{`) and treats the trailing `}` as a literal character. This is a well-known foot-gun and `shellcheck` does not currently flag it.

## Affected locations

Primary (actively observed):

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch.sh:692` — `_prefetch_repo_prs`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch.sh:888` — `_prefetch_repo_issues`

Same pattern, latent bug class, worth fixing in the same PR:

- `.agents/scripts/daytona-helper.sh:136` — `local body="${2:-{}}"` passed to `curl -d`. Non-empty caller body → corrupted JSON → API 400, silenced by `curl -f`.
- `.agents/scripts/muapi-helper.sh:686` — `local extra_payload="${1:-{}}"` piped to `jq '. + {…}'`. Non-empty caller payload → `jq` parse error → payload merge fails.
- `.agents/scripts/loop-common.sh:620` — `local evidence="${3:-{}}"`. Has a defensive `jq empty` check at line 623 that catches the invalid JSON and silently resets to `{}` — not a crash, but real caller evidence is discarded.

Git blame on the two `pulse-prefetch.sh` lines points to the Phase 7 extraction commit (`2510f135e`, 2026-04-12). The parent commit's `pulse-wrapper.sh` already contained the identical expansion at the corresponding sites — the extraction preserved the bug byte-identically rather than introducing it. The sibling `_prefetch_{prs,issues}_try_delta` helpers use the correct `"$2"` form, so the bug likely entered when a defensive default was retrofitted to the outer wrappers without realising the bash parser would swallow the closing `}`.

## Recommended fix

Two hygienic options, either is fine:

**A — escape the default braces** (minimal diff):

```bash
local cache_entry="${2:-\{\}}"
```

**B — explicit fallback** (more idiomatic, easier to read):

```bash
local cache_entry="${2:-}"
[[ -n "$cache_entry" ]] || cache_entry="{}"
```

Apply to all five sites listed above. Add a repo-wide grep guard (pre-commit or CI lint) against the literal regex `\$\{[0-9]+:-\{\}\}` to prevent regression.

### Suggested regression test

Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-delta-prefetch.sh`:

1. Call `_prefetch_repo_prs` and `_prefetch_repo_issues` directly with a non-empty `cache_entry` containing `last_prefetch`.
2. Assert that the subsequent `_prefetch_{prs,issues}_try_delta` call does NOT hit the "no timestamp" branch.
3. Assert at least one `"delta for .+: [0-9]+ changed (PRs|issues) merged into cache"` log line is produced.

## Impact

- 100% delta-failure rate on every pulse cycle whose fingerprint-check misses.
- Each failure runs a full `gh pr list --json ...` and `gh issue list --json ...` instead of a bounded `updated:>=<ts>` search — an order-of-magnitude-larger GraphQL cost per repo per cycle.
- The `gh` GraphQL primary quota is 5000 points/hour; with multiple pulse-enabled repos at ~60 cycles/hour, the budget saturates well before the rate-limit-aware paths (GH#18976) can help.
- The intended savings from GH#15286 (delta prefetch) have never been realised, and the further savings proposed in GH#18981 (batched org-level search) compound on top of delta that is currently broken.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.8.76 (latest: 3.8.76)
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: 2.90.0 (2026-04-16)
- **Runtime**: OpenCode (per `log-issue-helper.sh diagnostics`)

## Additional context

Related issues (not duplicates):

- GH#15286 — the `perf: delta prefetch with daily full sweep` initiative this bug breaks.
- GH#18981 — `feat(pulse): batch prefetch via org-level gh search` — open optimisation that assumes delta works.
- GH#19025 — `GraphQL budget optimisation roadmap` — the broader context.
- GH#18976 — `t2097: fail-loud on GraphQL rate limit exhaustion` — complementary, about detecting the symptom.

Bug is not deployed-only: source-of-truth file `~/Git/aidevops/.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch.sh` is identical to the deployed copy. Live pulse is still running with the bug active — evidence preserved.

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #19874 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #19874

**Parent issue:** #19874 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** Investigate: two sessions claimed t2377 without collision guard firing (race in claim-task-id.sh OR workflow bypass)
**Parent labels:** `bug,investigation,parent-task,tier:thinking,origin:interactive,framework,consolidation-in-progress`

> You do **NOT** need to read #19874. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #19874 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #19874:**

```bash
gh issue comment 19874 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 19874 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 19874 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #19874 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #19874** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

## Parent body (verbatim)

## Symptom

Two distinct tasks were filed under the same task ID (`t2377`) on 2026-04-19 within a ~20-minute window. Recovery: #19846 renamed to t2383 (commit/claim at `04:06Z`). Collision details in #19846#issuecomment-4275140235.

## What the repo history shows

```
08741df4e  2026-04-19 02:53:29Z  chore: claim t2377 [1316_12192]       ← Session A (legitimate claim)
#19846     2026-04-19 02:54:53Z  t2377: (Session A follow-up issue)
#19847     2026-04-19 03:14:43Z  t2377: fix(issue-sync) enrich ...     ← Session B uses same t2377
bc9a5b4e6  2026-04-19 03:16:48Z  t2377: brief and TODO entry ...       ← Session B brief commit
036ebed2d  2026-04-19 03:18:53Z  chore: claim t2378 [53399_27428]      ← Session B then claims t2378
a37573afe  2026-04-19 03:22:53Z  plan: file t2378 — markdownlint ...   ← Session B uses t2378 for DIFFERENT work
0b6ea692c  2026-04-19 03:41:05Z  PR #19849 merged (t2377 enrich-path)
```

**Session B used `t2377` in an issue and brief without a corresponding `chore: claim t2377` commit.** Only one claim commit for t2377 exists in git history (`08741df4e`, Session A). Session B then legitimately claimed `t2378` but used it for an unrelated task (markdownlint refactor), while their earlier `t2377` work (enrich-path) was merged without ever being atomically claimed.

## Two hypotheses

1. **Session B skipped `claim-task-id.sh` entirely** and hardcoded `t2377` from a stale counter read (either from a cached value, a prior session, or reading the local counter file without going through the CAS path). This is a workflow violation, not a helper bug.

2. **`claim-task-id.sh` has a race window** where two sessions can both successfully CAS the same counter value if their push-retry logic overlaps. Session A's `[1316_12192]` CAS token succeeded; Session B may have had its own CAS attempt succeed too if the retry loop picks up a stale `remote counter` value between `git fetch` and `git push --force-with-lease`.

## What evidence would discriminate

- **Check Session B's session database** (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` or `~/.claude/projects/`) for the string `claim-task-id` around 03:14-03:18Z — if it was invoked and returned a result, hypothesis 2 is supported; if not, hypothesis 1.
- **Re-read `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh`** for the CAS critical section — specifically the sequence `fetch → read counter → increment → push --force-with-lease` and whether the `force-with-lease` reference matches the fetched value or a re-read.
- **Check for concurrency primitives** — does the helper use `flock` or similar local-machine mutex? If two sessions are on the same machine, a filesystem-level lock would prevent the race entirely.

## What to do (if hypothesis 2 is confirmed)

- Add `flock` around the counter-read-increment-push sequence (machine-local mutex sufficient for single-developer setups).
- For cross-machine safety, use `git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/main:<sha-just-fetched>` AND verify post-push that the counter still matches the claimed value; roll back and retry if not.
- Add a post-claim verification step that re-fetches and confirms the specific claim commit is on origin/main, not just "any push succeeded".

## What to do (if hypothesis 1 is confirmed)

- Enforce `claim-task-id.sh` as the only entry point via:
  - A pre-commit hook that rejects `chore: claim t*` commits not produced by the helper.
  - A pre-push hook that rejects task ID references in commit messages / issue/PR titles without a matching `chore: claim` commit on the branch.
- Existing `task-id-collision-check.yml` CI workflow (per AGENTS.md t2047) partially covers this but didn't catch the race.

## Priority

Low-frequency recurrence (one observed instance in framework history) but HIGH cost when it happens (hour+ of manual untangling, audit trail pollution, rename workflow, memory updates). Worth investigating before the next collision.

### Comment 1 — @marcusquinn at 2026-04-19T16:26:13Z

## Investigation: Hypothesis 1 confirmed + newly identified gap

I read `claim-task-id.sh` end-to-end and cross-referenced with the existing `task-id-collision-guard.sh` hook and CI workflow. The CAS implementation is sound — this was a workflow bypass, not a helper race.

### Evidence for Hypothesis 1 (Session B skipped the helper)

From the body's git log:

```text
08741df4e  02:53:29Z  chore: claim t2377 [1316_12192]       ← Session A (CAS commit exists)
bc9a5b4e6  03:16:48Z  t2377: brief and TODO entry ...       ← Session B uses t2377 WITHOUT a claim commit
036ebed2d  03:18:53Z  chore: claim t2378 [53399_27428]      ← Session B THEN claims t2378 properly
```

Session B produced **no** `chore: claim t2377 [...]` commit. If `allocate_counter_cas()` had returned `2377` to Session B, it would have committed one — the helper's commit message format at line 610 is the only legitimate source of that subject. Two minutes later Session B invoked the helper cleanly for `t2378`, producing the expected CAS commit. So Session B didn't accidentally race the helper; Session B bypassed it entirely for their first piece of work and used it correctly for their second.

### CAS audit (rules out Hypothesis 2)

`allocate_counter_cas()` at `claim-task-id.sh:581`:

1. `_cas_fetch_and_pin` reads `.task-counter` from `${REMOTE_NAME}/${COUNTER_BRANCH}` AND captures the parent SHA atomically (GH#19689 fix — line 496 comment enforces "all subsequent reads MUST use pinned_sha").
2. Commit built via `git commit-tree` with PID + `$RANDOM` nonce to prevent commit-identity collision (line 600-606, also GH#19689).
3. Pushed with `--force-with-lease` against `pinned_sha` — if any session committed between the fetch and push, the lease check fails and we retry.
4. Retry loop in `allocate_online()` at `claim-task-id.sh:630` allows 30 attempts with exponential backoff + jitter (lines 635-642).

A genuine CAS race would surface as BOTH sessions having valid `chore: claim t2377 [nonce]` commits in git history with different nonces (the first push wins, the second must retry and get t2378). We see only Session A's commit, so Session B's code path never entered the CAS loop.

### Gap identified in the existing collision guard

`task-id-collision-guard.sh` ("invented — i.e., greater than the current .task-counter on the merge base") catches the **invention** case: a commit subject like `t2999: foo` when the counter is at 2390 — clearly fabricated.

It does NOT catch the **reuse** case: Session B's `t2377: brief and TODO entry` commit references a t-ID that was already claimed (the counter was at 2378+ by then). The guard sees "t2377 is not greater than counter, someone has claimed it" and passes, but never verifies that the claim commit is on the same branch / authored by the same session. That's the actual gap: the guard answers "does this t-ID exist?" but not "did THIS branch claim this t-ID?".

### Recommended decomposition (for the parent-task)

**Phase 1 — harden the collision guard** (tier:simple):
- In `_check_subject_ids()`, for every t-ID referenced in a commit subject outside the helper's own `chore: claim tNNN [nonce]` pattern, require a matching `chore: claim tNNN [nonce]` commit to exist on the current branch (merge-base..HEAD). Absence = reject. This catches the reuse case directly.
- Bypass: `TASK_ID_GUARD_DISABLE=1` (already defined, line 38).

**Phase 2 — defence in depth** (tier:simple):
- Add a machine-local `flock` around the CAS critical section in `allocate_counter_cas()`. Not required for correctness (git push is authoritative), but cuts retry cost when two agents race on the same host — which is a common multi-session concurrency mode.

**Phase 3 — detection telemetry** (tier:simple):
- Log every successful `allocate_counter_cas` with `pid`, `session_id` (if available from env), `claimed_id`, `nonce`, `attempt_number` to `~/.aidevops/logs/task-claim.log`. When the guard rejects a reused-without-claim subject, cross-reference against this log to confirm whether the original claim came from a sibling session on the same host (typo fix / copy-paste) vs a genuine leak.

### Priority confirmation

I agree with the body's "low-frequency, high-cost" assessment. Phase 1 alone would have caught the t2377 incident — the guard is one conditional away from covering this case. Phase 2/3 are defence-in-depth and can ship independently.

### Dispatchability for next worker

- **Phase 1** is tier:simple: one file (`task-id-collision-guard.sh`), one function edit, reference pattern at lines 100-250 (existing `_check_subject_ids`), regression fixture = minimal synthetic git history with Session A claim + Session B reuse.
- **Phase 2** is tier:standard: one file (`claim-task-id.sh`), new wrapper around `allocate_counter_cas`, with portable flock (macOS lacks `flock` binary — use `mkdir` or Python one-liner). Reference pattern: pulse-wrapper uses `mkdir` locks.
- **Phase 3** is tier:simple: add log line + document the log path.

None of the phases require the `#parent` tag to be kept on THIS issue once Phase 1 ships — the guard fix alone addresses the root cause. Phases 2-3 are tracking improvements.

## Parent Task Needs Decomposition

This issue carries the `parent-task` label, which unconditionally blocks pulse dispatch (see `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` → `PARENT_TASK_BLOCKED`). It also has **zero filed children** — no `## Children`, `## Sub-tasks`, or `## Child issues` section with `#NNNN` references, and no GraphQL sub-issue graph.

Under these two conditions the issue cannot make progress on its own. Workers won't pick it up (dispatch blocked), no completion sweep can fire (no children to check), and nothing else nudges it forward. Without decomposition it will sit here silently forever.

**Two paths forward — pick one:**

1. **Decompose into children.** File the specific implementation tasks as separate issues, then edit this parent body to include a section like:

   ```
   ## Children

   - t2XXX / #NNNN — first specific task
   - t2YYY / #MMMM — second specific task
   ```

   The next pulse cycle will detect the children via `reconcile_completed_parent_tasks` and auto-close this parent once all listed children are closed.

2. **Drop the parent-task label.** If this issue is actually a single unit of work (not a roadmap tracker), remove the `parent-task` label so the pulse can dispatch it directly:

   ```
   gh issue edit 19874 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --remove-label parent-task
   ```

See `.agents/AGENTS.md` → "Parent / meta tasks" (t1986 / t2211) for the full rule. Parent-task is for epics and roadmap trackers that will never be implemented as a single unit — only their children will.

title: consolidated: feat(issue-sync) detect umbrella-style parent-tasks and link children via sub_issues API
body:
_Supersedes #19778 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn -->

## What

Add parent-side detection to `backfill-sub-issues` in `issue-sync-relationships.sh`: when iterating all issues, check if the issue is a `parent-task` (by label) and, if so, parse its body for a `## Children` section (and aliases: `## Child Issues`, `## Sub-issues`, `## Phases`) and link every `#NNN` / `GH#NNN` reference in that section as a sub-issue via the GitHub sub_issues API.

## Why

- Umbrella-style parents never get their children linked programmatically — the only audit trail is prose in the body. The existing `backfill-sub-issues` path runs CHILD-side only (`_backfill_one_issue` calls `_detect_parent_from_gh_state` on each candidate child and links upward), matching three patterns: `tNNN.M` dot-notation title, `Parent:` line in body, `Blocked by:` referencing a parent-task-labeled issue. None of those patterns match the umbrella style where the PARENT carries the children list and the children never reference the parent.
- `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh::_try_close_parent_tracker` (t2244/GH#19762 target) needs the authoritative sub-issue graph to avoid false closures. Without umbrella-side detection, it falls back to a too-permissive body regex and mis-closes umbrellas on unrelated `#NNN` prose mentions (canonical: t2244/GH#19762 premature-close of #19734).
- GitHub UI shows sub-issue progress in the sidebar; unlinked children look like orphans.
- Framework principle: the harness should wire relationships at creation/sync time, not require an agent to remember to POST manually.

## Tier

### Tier checklist (verify before assigning)

- [x] **2 or fewer files to modify?** — primary edit is `issue-sync-relationships.sh`; secondary is docstring in `issue-sync-helper.sh`; test file is a third but it is test-only
- [ ] **Every target file under 500 lines?** — `issue-sync-relationships.sh` is likely >500 lines
- [ ] **Exact `oldString`/`newString` for every edit?** — no, this requires section-parsing and regex design
- [ ] **No judgment or design decisions?** — regex choice and section-heading alias matching are judgment calls
- [x] **No error handling or fallback logic to design?**
- [x] **No cross-package or cross-module changes?**
- [x] **Estimate 1h or less?**
- [x] **4 or fewer acceptance criteria?** — 7 acceptance criteria

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Single-file change in existing helper, extends well-tested pattern, has clear acceptance criteria and verification command. Not tier:simple because the section-parsing and regex choice are judgment calls that benefit from Sonnet review. Not tier:thinking because there is a clear existing pattern to follow.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-relationships.sh:619-665` — extend `_backfill_one_issue` OR add a sibling `_backfill_parent_children($parent_num, $repo)` that runs when the issue carries the `parent-task` label.
- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-relationships.sh:676-730` — in `cmd_backfill_sub_issues`, fetch labels alongside title/body and dispatch to child-side or parent-side logic.
- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh:1497-1503` — update docstring to document the new parent-side detection pattern.
- **EXTEND:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-backfill-sub-issues.sh` — add cases for umbrella-style parent with `## Children` section listing 4 children. Mirror the existing Class B test harness.

### Implementation Steps

1. **Add `_backfill_parent_children` function** in `issue-sync-relationships.sh`, modelled on the child-side detection at line 619. The new function should:
   - Accept parent issue number + repo.
   - Receive the parent body (already fetched in the outer loop — pass it in to avoid double-fetch).
   - Parse the body for a `## Children` heading (case-insensitive, allow `## Child Issues`, `## Sub-issues`, `## Phases` as aliases).
   - In that section, extract every `#NNN` / `GH#NNN` reference (anchored to line start with `-` list marker OR markdown table cell to avoid prose matches).
   - For each extracted number, resolve its node ID via `_cached_node_id` and call `_gh_add_sub_issue($parent_node, $child_node)`.
   - Return count of links made (for summary output).

2. **Extraction regex candidate** — validate against both umbrella styles observed:
   - #19734 body: `| HIGH | t2229 | #19735 | ...` (markdown table)
   - #19736 body: `- t2229 / #19738 — CI workflow cascade-vulnerability linter` (markdown list)

   Table-cell regex needs to tolerate both:

   ```bash
   rg -oE '^[[:space:]]*[-|][^-|]*#([0-9]+)' | sed -E 's/.*#([0-9]+).*/\1/'
   ```

3. **Wire parent-side dispatch** in `cmd_backfill_sub_issues` (line 676-730) — fetch labels alongside title/body and call `_backfill_parent_children` when the `parent-task` label is present.

4. **Self-healing hook**: Run parent-side backfill from the existing pulse reconcile phase `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:1236` (already wired to call `backfill-sub-issues`). No new scheduling needed — the addition just widens what the periodic pass detects.

5. **Update docstring** in `issue-sync-helper.sh:1497-1503` to document the new parent-side detection pattern.

6. **Add test case** in `test-backfill-sub-issues.sh` — fixture umbrella issue body with `## Children` section + 3-4 children issues; assert all get linked. Mirror the existing Class B test harness.

### Verification

```bash
# Dry-run on a known umbrella parent
issue-sync-helper.sh backfill-sub-issues --issue 19734 --dry-run

# Verify idempotence
issue-sync-helper.sh backfill-sub-issues --issue 19734
issue-sync-helper.sh backfill-sub-issues --issue 19734  # second run should be no-op

# Confirm sub-issue graph
gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/19734/sub_issues" --jq '[.[] | .number] | sort'

# Run tests
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-backfill-sub-issues.sh

# ShellCheck
shellcheck .agents/scripts/issue-sync-relationships.sh
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `issue-sync-helper.sh backfill-sub-issues --issue 19734 --dry-run` reports 7 children that would be linked (all of #19735, #19737, #19743, #19744, #19751, #19752, #19753).
- [ ] Without `--dry-run`, the same command produces `sub_issues_summary.total = 7` on #19734.
- [ ] Idempotent — running twice doesn't error or duplicate.
- [ ] Existing child-side detection still works for the three legacy patterns (dot-notation, `Parent:` line, `Blocked by:` with parent-task label). No regression on `test-backfill-sub-issues.sh` Class A + Class B cases.
- [ ] New test case: fixture umbrella issue body with `## Children` section + 3 children issues; assert all 3 get linked.
- [ ] Prose body text like "see #19678" or "resolved by PR #19680" OUTSIDE the `## Children` section does NOT produce a false link.
- [ ] Verification command: `gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/19734/sub_issues" --jq '[.[] | .number] | sort'` returns the child list.

## Context & Decisions

- **Discovery (per @marcusquinn, 2026-04-18):** Found during board-clearing session after observing parent-tasks #19734 and #19736 had zero GitHub sub-issue links despite both bodies containing explicit `## Children` sections listing 7 and 4 children respectively. Manual `POST /repos/:owner/:repo/issues/:num/sub_issues` with child `id` (integer) linked all children cleanly.
- **Root cause (per @marcusquinn):** The existing `backfill-sub-issues` path runs child-side only. `_backfill_one_issue` calls `_detect_parent_from_gh_state` on each candidate child and links upward when it finds one of three patterns. None match the umbrella style where the parent carries the children list.
- **Approach chosen:** Add a sibling function `_backfill_parent_children` rather than modifying the existing child-side function, keeping both detection paths clean and independently testable.
- **Section heading aliases:** `## Children`, `## Child Issues`, `## Sub-issues`, `## Phases` — all observed or anticipated in umbrella-style parents. Case-insensitive match.
- **Regex scope constraint:** Only match `#NNN` references inside the children section, anchored to markdown list items (`-`) or table cells (`|`) to avoid prose false positives.
- **Brief-only PR already merged (per @marcusquinn, Comment 1):** PR #19781 landed the brief for this task only, not the implementation. The `status:done` label from auto-completion was incorrect — the merged PR used `Ref #19778` (not a closing keyword), meaning the issue should have stayed open.
- **Data-loss incident (per @marcusquinn, Comments 2-3):** Issue content was temporarily destroyed by the t2377 enrichment data-loss bug. Content was preserved in `todo/tasks/t2349-brief.md` on disk. Reopened after the 5-layer defence fix merged (PR #19876, deployed 2026-04-19 05:42 UTC).
- **Canonical parents needing this fix:** #19734 (v3.8.71 retrospective, 7 children), #19736 (harness self-inflicted CI failure class, 4 children). Already wired manually during the filing session — test by running backfill and confirming idempotence.

## Related

- GH#19762 / t2244 (parent) — the `_try_close_parent_tracker` bug that misfires when the sub-issue graph is empty; this task addresses the upstream "graph is empty" root cause by populating it.
- GH#19093 / t2114 — original backfill-sub-issues feature (child-side detection); this task is the Phase 2 extension.
- #19734 — v3.8.71 retrospective umbrella (7 children, manually wired, test target for idempotence).
- #19736 — harness self-inflicted CI failure class umbrella (4 children, manually wired).

## Contributors

cc @marcusquinn

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-relationships.sh:619-665` — existing child-side `_backfill_one_issue` (reference pattern)
- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-relationships.sh:676-730` — `cmd_backfill_sub_issues` outer loop
- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh:1497-1503` — docstring for backfill-sub-issues
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-backfill-sub-issues.sh` — existing test harness
- `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:1236` — existing wiring that calls backfill-sub-issues

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Research/read | 15m | Read existing `_backfill_one_issue` pattern at :619 |
| Implementation | 45m | New function + wiring in outer loop + docstring |
| Testing | 30m | New test case + regression run |
| **Total** | **~1.5h** | |
