title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #18981 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #18981

**Parent issue:** #18981 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** feat(pulse): batch prefetch via org-level gh search to reduce GraphQL consumption ~50x
**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:standard,consolidation-in-progress`

> You do **NOT** need to read #18981. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #18981 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #18981:**

```bash
gh issue comment 18981 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 18981 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 18981 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #18981 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #18981** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

## Parent body (verbatim)

## Problem

`pulse-prefetch.sh` loops through every pulse-enabled repo and runs individual `gh issue list --repo $slug` / `gh pr list --repo $slug` calls. Each of these uses GraphQL internally via the `gh` CLI. With 16+ repos, a single pulse cycle makes **~192 GraphQL calls** in the prefetch phase alone:

| Call site | Function | Line | Per-repo calls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_prefetch_needs_full_sweep` | issue list + pr list | ~135, ~138 | 2 |
| `_prefetch_needs_full_sweep` | issue search + pr search (delta check) | ~222, ~231 | 2 |
| `_prefetch_prs_try_delta` / full | pr list | ~464, ~603 | 1-2 |
| `_prefetch_prs_enrich_checks` | pr list (statusCheckRollup) | ~513 | 1 |
| `_prefetch_repo_daily_cap` | pr list --state all | ~652 | 1 |
| `_prefetch_issues_try_delta` / full | issue list | ~722, ~784 | 1-2 |
| `prefetch_triage_review_status` | issue list (NMR label) | ~1765 | 1 |
| `prefetch_needs_info_replies` | issue list (needs-info label) | ~1872 | 1 |

At 5-min intervals (12 cycles/hr), that's **~2300 GraphQL calls/hr** — nearly half the 5000/hr budget before any dispatch, merge, or triage work happens. Observed repeatedly: GraphQL hits 0/5000 while REST (core) sits at 3997/5000 unused.

When GraphQL is exhausted, every `gh issue list` fails, prefetch returns empty data (`prs=0 issues=0`), and the entire pulse cycle does nothing — no dispatch, no merge, no triage. The cycle still burns 3+ minutes holding the instance lock.

## Proposed Solution: org-level `gh search` batch prefetch

### Core idea

Group pulse-enabled repos by owner (from `repos.json`), run **one `gh search issues --owner X`** and **one `gh search prs --owner X`** per owner, then split results by `repository.nameWithOwner` into per-slug cache files. Existing per-repo functions read the cache first, falling back to individual `gh` calls only on cache miss.

### Measured impact

Tested live against the current repo set (16 pulse-enabled repos across 3 owners):

```
$ time gh search issues --owner Ultimate-Multisite --state open --limit 200 \
    --json number,title,labels,updatedAt,assignees,repository | \
    jq 'group_by(.repository.nameWithOwner) | length'
42    # repos with open issues

real  0m5.106s
```

**One call (5 seconds) replaces 15+ individual `gh issue list --repo` calls.** The output includes number, title, labels (with names), assignees (with logins), updatedAt, and repository — all fields the prefetch consumers need.

### API budget comparison

| Approach | Calls/cycle | API bucket | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Current** (per-repo `gh issue/pr list`) | ~192 | GraphQL | 5000/hr |
| **Proposed** (`gh search --owner X`) | ~6 (3 owners × {issues,prs}) | Search | 30/min (1800/hr) |
| Enrichment (statusCheckRollup, daily cap) | ~16 | GraphQL | stays on GraphQL |

Net GraphQL reduction: **~192 → ~16 per cycle** (enrichment-only). The bulk list moves entirely to the Search API, which has its own separate rate limit (30/min) and is currently at 0 usage.

### Shape compatibility

`gh search issues --owner X --json number,title,labels,updatedAt,assignees,repository` returns:

```json
{
  "number": 813,
  "title": "t164: Seamless PHP+JS abilities",
  "labels": [{"name":"enhancement","color":"EDEDED",...}],
  "assignees": [{"login":"superdav42",...}],
  "updatedAt": "2026-04-08T18:46:10Z",
  "repository": {"name":"gratis-ai-agent","nameWithOwner":"Ultimate-Multisite/gratis-ai-agent"}
}
```

After `del(.repository)`, this matches the shape of `gh issue list --repo X --json number,title,labels,updatedAt,assignees`. Drop-in compatible for downstream consumers.

### What `gh search` does NOT support

- `reviewDecision` / `statusCheckRollup` for PRs — the existing `_prefetch_prs_enrich_checks` per-PR enrichment pass stays as-is
- `headRefName` for PRs — not used in the bulk list, only in merge pass (which already does per-PR `gh pr view`)
- `--state all` for daily cap counting — daily cap still needs per-repo `gh pr list --state all` (or switch to `gh search prs --owner X --merged >=today`)

These are already separate enrichment/utility passes in the current code architecture. Only the bulk issue/PR list needs batching.

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1: Standalone batch prefetch helper

Create `.agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh` with subcommands:

- `refresh` — group pulse-enabled repos by owner (from repos.json), run one `gh search` per owner per kind (issues/prs), split results into per-slug cache files at `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/supervisor/batch-prefetch/{kind}-{owner}--{repo}.json`
- `cache-path --kind issues|prs --slug owner/repo` — return cache file path if fresh (within TTL), exit 1 if miss/stale. Used by pulse-prefetch.sh to check for cached data.
- `clear` — wipe cache
- `status` — show cache ages, counts

### Step 2: Wire into pulse-prefetch.sh

- Add `PULSE_BATCH_PREFETCH_ENABLED` flag (default: `1`, read from settings.json `supervisor.batch_prefetch_enabled`)
- At the top of `prefetch_state`, call `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh refresh` once
- In `_prefetch_repo_issues` (full-sweep path, ~line 784): before calling `gh issue list --repo $slug`, check `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh cache-path --kind issues --slug $slug`. If exit 0, read the cache file instead. If exit 1, fall back to existing per-repo `gh issue list`.
- Same for `_prefetch_repo_prs` (~line 603)
- Same for `prefetch_triage_review_status` (~line 1765) and `prefetch_needs_info_replies` (~line 1872) — these filter by label, so either: (a) filter the cached full list in jq, or (b) let them fall through to per-repo calls (they're only 2 calls each, not the hot path)

### Step 3: Delta cache compatibility

The current delta prefetch (`_prefetch_issues_try_delta`, `_prefetch_prs_try_delta`) merges recently-updated items into a cached full list. The batch prefetch replaces the full-sweep path, not the delta path. On cycles where delta is used (non-full-sweep), the existing delta logic runs as-is against the per-slug cache from the last batch refresh. The `last_prefetch` timestamp in the prefetch cache should be updated when batch refresh writes a new per-slug file.

### Files to modify

- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh` — standalone helper (~300 lines)
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch.sh`
  - `prefetch_state` (~line 1111): add batch refresh call before parallel per-repo fetches
  - `_prefetch_repo_issues` (~line 784): add cache-path check before `gh issue list`
  - `_prefetch_repo_prs` (~line 603): add cache-path check before `gh pr list`
  - `_prefetch_needs_full_sweep` (~lines 135, 138, 222, 231): skip the per-repo "did anything change?" check when batch cache is fresh (the batch refresh already fetched the current state)
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — add `PULSE_BATCH_PREFETCH_ENABLED` to bootstrap constants
- **EDIT**: `.agents/configs/settings-schema.json` (if exists) — add `supervisor.batch_prefetch_enabled` field

### Verification

1. Run `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh refresh` and verify per-slug cache files match `gh issue list --repo $slug` output (field names, counts, label filtering)
2. Run a full pulse cycle with batch prefetch enabled, check `pulse.log` for: `[pulse-prefetch] Using batch cache for $slug (N issues)` messages
3. Compare `gh api rate_limit` before and after a cycle — GraphQL usage should drop from ~192 to ~16; Search usage should increase by ~6
4. Disable batch prefetch (`PULSE_BATCH_PREFETCH_ENABLED=0`), verify pulse falls back to per-repo calls cleanly
5. Artificially create a stale cache (TTL=1, sleep 2), verify fallback to per-repo

### Rollback

Feature-flagged: set `supervisor.batch_prefetch_enabled: false` in settings.json or `PULSE_BATCH_PREFETCH_ENABLED=0` env var. Zero regression risk — per-repo calls remain as the fallback path.

### Search API rate limit note

The Search API limit is 30 requests/min (not per hour). With 3 owners × 2 kinds = 6 calls per cycle at 5-min intervals, that's 6 calls every 5 minutes — well within the 30/min budget. Even at the old 2-min interval with 10 owners, 20 calls/2min = 10/min, still safe.

## Substantive comments (verbatim, in chronological order)

### Comment 1 — @alex-solovyev at 2026-04-14T19:12:30Z

## Review: Needs Changes

### Issue Validation

| Check | Status | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| Reproducible | Yes | GraphQL rate limit exhaustion is a documented, observed problem |
| Not duplicate | No | t2098 (just merged) targets the same problem — "reduce GraphQL consumption ~50%" — and t2097 adds fail-loud on exhaustion |
| Actual bug | Yes | Excessive GraphQL consumption is real, but root cause may already be addressed |
| In scope | Yes | Pulse efficiency is core framework concern |

**Root Cause:** The contributor themselves identified in the comments that "running both cron and systemd schedule every 2 mins doing duplicate work was probably the real cause of the problem." Combined with t2098 (skip prefetch for idle repos, ~50% reduction) and t2097 (fail-loud on exhaustion), the immediate pressure may already be resolved. The batch prefetch proposal optimises a path whose call volume was inflated by duplicate scheduling — the post-fix baseline needs measurement before adding architectural complexity.

### Scope & Recommendation

- **Scope creep:** High — the proposal introduces a new helper, a new cache layer, a new API surface (Search), a feature flag, settings-schema changes, and modifications to 4+ files in one of the most critical pulse subsystems. The maintainer explicitly flagged this: "just tell me the problem, so i can explore ALL options for solutions."
- **Complexity tier:** `tier:thinking` — architectural change to a core subsystem with concurrency, caching, and API budget implications
- **Decision:** REQUEST CHANGES
- **Recommended labels:** `needs-info`, `enhancement`
- **Implementation guidance:**
  - **Measure first:** After t2098 + duplicate-scheduling fix have run for 48h, capture `gh api rate_limit` snapshots across several pulse cycles. If GraphQL usage is now sustainable, close this as unnecessary. The contributor's 192-call estimate was under duplicate scheduling — the real number is likely ~96 post-dedup, minus ~50% from t2098 idle-repo skip = ~48.
  - **Separate problem from solution:** The issue body is 90% implementation plan and 10% problem statement. Per the maintainer's comment, reframe as a problem report with measurements, not a prescriptive architecture. The `gh search` approach has trade-offs not fully explored: Search API indexing delay (items may not appear for seconds-to-minutes after creation), `--limit 200` cap per call (repos with 200+ open issues truncate silently), and Search API's own secondary rate limits under heavy use.
  - **If still needed after measurement:** the batch approach is sound in principle but should be a standalone optimisation issue scoped to just the new helper + one integration point, not a 4-file refactor. Feature flag is good. Start with `refresh` + `cache-path` only; wire into `_prefetch_repo_issues`/`_prefetch_repo_prs` as the single integration seam.

---

### Comment 2 — @marcusquinn at 2026-04-14T23:47:19Z

@superdav42 not a big deal, but sometimes there's more than one way to solve something, and this one i think should be solved from some parallel work.

I'm just getting a few race issues where i have some issues that yoyo one solution for another problem and back again, or parallel solutions for the same problem that make the logic more complex to maintain, or we're trying to do too much with something, and the symptom is the indicator to unwind an approach and rebuild to scale better.

It's all valuable, though, as the ai-created issues i can then use as examples to try get the agent writing them to also think about these things for us.

It's just a heads-up, that we might already have solutions or options in the pipeline, including things i just haven't got to yet, so treat each issue as more of a log of evidence, than a patch brief.

---

### Comment 3 — @marcusquinn at 2026-04-14T23:59:47Z

## Relationship to GH#18976 (closed) and GH#19025 (roadmap)

The immediate symptom this issue describes — GraphQL exhaustion causing silent no-op cycles — is fixed:

- **t2097** (PR #18983): fail-loud detection + cycle abort at all 5 prefetch sites
- **t2098** (PR #18985): idle repo skip — on cache-hit, reuse cached data instead of 6 expensive `gh` calls per idle repo

Budget went from ~840 base calls/hr to ~420/hr for prefetch. But during heavy dispatch (10+ workers), worker-side `gh` calls push total consumption to ~3800/hr against a 5000/hr budget. At 14 repos this is workable. At 50+ it won't be.

**This issue (#18981) remains the correct long-term answer for the bulk-listing layer.** It's now linked to the scaling roadmap at GH#19025.

---

## Architectural vision: layered prefetch with single normalization boundary

The batch approach proposed here, the idle skip shipped in t2098, the delta cache from GH#15286, and the state fingerprint from t2041 are not alternatives — they're **layers in the same cache hierarchy**, each eliminating work at a different level. The ideal design composes them:

### Cache hierarchy (ordered by cost, cheapest first)

```
L1: State fingerprint (t2041)
    Cost: 0 API calls (local hash comparison)
    Skips: entire repo when fingerprint matches
    Already shipped.

L2: Idle skip (t2098)
    Cost: 0 API calls (reads L4 cache)
    Skips: 6 expensive per-repo calls, replays cached data
    Always runs checks enrichment for repos with cached PRs > 0.
    Already shipped.

L3: Batch prefetch (#18981 — THIS ISSUE)
    Cost: 2 calls per owner (gh search issues + prs)
    Uses: Search API bucket (30/min = 1800/hr, currently at 0 usage)
    Replaces: N individual gh issue/pr list calls on GraphQL
    Populates the same cache that L1 and L2 read from.

L4: Delta prefetch (GH#15286)
    Cost: 2 calls per repo (updated:>ISO search)
    Falls back to full fetch only when delta detects changes.
    Already shipped.

L5: Per-PR enrichment (existing)
    Cost: 1 call per repo with open PRs
    Fetches: statusCheckRollup, reviewDecision (not in search results)
    Stays on GraphQL — this is irreducible.
```

### How they compose

On each cycle, for each repo:

1. **L1** checks fingerprint. Match → **L2** replays cache → done (0 API calls).
2. Fingerprint miss → **L3** batch-fetches all repos for this owner in one Search API call, splits by slug, updates cache.
3. **L4** delta-merges any per-repo changes that arrived between batch fetch and now (race window).
4. **L5** enriches PRs with `statusCheckRollup` / `reviewDecision` (GraphQL, per-PR).

At 50 repos across 5 owners: **10 Search API calls + ~5 enrichment calls** per cycle, regardless of repo count. GraphQL drops to enrichment-only. Total budget consumption becomes proportional to active PRs, not repo count.

### Single normalization boundary (the maintenance key)

The biggest drift risk is field-mapping between `gh search` output and `gh issue/pr list` output. Both return `number`, `title`, `labels`, `assignees`, `updatedAt` — but `gh search` adds `repository` and omits PR-specific fields.

**Rule**: normalize at ingestion, once. The batch fetcher strips `repository`, adds any missing fields with null defaults, and writes the same cache schema that `_prefetch_cache_set` already uses. All downstream consumers read the cache — never raw API responses. Field-mapping lives in exactly one function. If the shape drifts, one function breaks, one test catches it, one fix resolves it.

### What this means for #18981 implementation

The proposal in this issue is architecturally correct. The refinements from our investigation:

1. **Layer it on top of t2098, don't replace it.** The idle skip is the L1/L2 fast path that avoids even the batch call for unchanged repos. The batch call is the L3 path for when something HAS changed — it just does it in bulk instead of per-repo.

2. **Normalize at the boundary.** Add a `_normalize_search_result_to_cache_schema()` function that maps `gh search` output to the existing cache entry schema. One function, one test, no downstream changes.

3. **Keep the fail-loud pattern.** Every new API call site must use `_pulse_gh_err_is_rate_limit` and `_pulse_mark_rate_limited` (t2097). The Search API has its own rate limit (30/min) — detect it the same way.

4. **Add budget accounting.** Extend `_PULSE_HEALTH_*` counters: `graphql_calls`, `search_calls`, `cache_hits`. Without instrumentation, every future optimization is a guess.

5. **`reviewDecision` stays on GraphQL.** The Search API doesn't return it. The checks enrichment pass (L5) is irreducible. This is fine — it's 1 call per repo with open PRs, not per repo total.

### Scaling math

| Repos | Current (no batch) | With full stack |
|-------|-------------------|-----------------|
| 14 | ~420/hr GraphQL | ~70/hr GraphQL + 12/hr Search |
| 50 | ~1500/hr GraphQL | ~100/hr GraphQL + 20/hr Search |
| 200 | ~6000/hr (EXHAUSTED) | ~250/hr GraphQL + 40/hr Search |

At 200 repos, the current design breaks. With the full cache hierarchy, it's comfortable. The scaling bottleneck shifts from API budget to cycle duration (iterating 200 repos sequentially) — which is a different problem with a different solution (parallel batch processing, already partially in place).

---

**Recommendation**: implement #18981 as the L3 layer when repo count approaches 30 or when worker-side consumption regularly pushes above 3500/hr. The t2097/t2098 fixes buy time. The architecture above is the target state — each layer is independently shippable and testable.

---

### Comment 4 — @marcusquinn at 2026-04-19T16:05:24Z

## Implementation review — approved with refinements

### Verified claims

- **Search API uses separate budget**: confirmed. 3 search calls consumed 0 GraphQL points. Search budget is 30/min (resets per-minute, not per-hour).
- **Field shape is compatible**: confirmed. `gh search issues --owner X --json number,title,labels,updatedAt,assignees,repository` returns the same fields as `gh issue list --repo X --json number,title,labels,updatedAt,assignees` after `del(.repository)`.
- **Performance**: one `gh search issues --owner marcusquinn` call takes ~1.2s and returns all open issues across 8 repos. Replaces 8 individual `gh issue list` calls.

### What shipped since this issue was filed

Three changes that the implementation must integrate with (not replace):

| Change | What it does | Integration requirement |
|--------|-------------|----------------------|
| **t2097** (PR #18983) | Rate-limit error detection + cycle abort at all prefetch sites | **Extend** `_pulse_gh_err_is_rate_limit` patterns to cover Search API rate-limit errors (`"Search rate limit exceeded"`, HTTP 422 secondary) |
| **t2098** (PR #18985) | Idle repo skip on cache-hit — reuses cached data | **Layer on top**: batch fetch populates the cache that the idle skip reads. On fingerprint match, idle skip fires before batch fetch runs → 0 API calls for unchanged repos |
| **t2173** (PR #19626) | Live GraphQL budget probe — cross-checks classifier against `rateLimit{remaining}` before committing abort flag | **Not needed for Search API** — it has its own separate budget, and a false positive on the search bucket just means one skipped batch, not a cycle abort |

### Refined implementation plan

The issue's plan is correct. Refinements to account for shipped work:

1. **`_prefetch_single_repo_idle_skip` (t2098) is the L1/L2 fast path** — it must run BEFORE the batch cache is consulted. The execution order in `_prefetch_single_repo` should be:
   ```
   if cache_hit → _prefetch_single_repo_idle_skip (0 API calls, done)
   elif batch_cache_fresh → read batch cache (0 API calls, done)
   else → per-repo gh call (existing fallback)
   ```

2. **Normalization function** — add `_normalize_search_to_prefetch_schema()` that:
   - Strips `.repository` from each item
   - Adds `createdAt: null` (not in search results, not needed for dispatch — only daily cap uses it, and daily cap stays on per-repo GraphQL)
   - Adds `author: null` for issues (used by needs-info scan, but `_prefetch_cached_label_count_is_zero` already skips repos with 0 matching)
   - Writes the normalized result to the same cache schema that `_prefetch_cache_set` uses

3. **Batch cache location** — use `${PULSE_PREFETCH_CACHE_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops/logs/batch-prefetch/}` not a nested `supervisor/` path. Keep it alongside the existing `pulse-prefetch-cache.json`.

4. **Batch cache TTL** — same as `PULSE_PREFETCH_FULL_SWEEP_INTERVAL` (24h default). The batch is the new "full sweep". Delta prefetch (GH#15286) handles inter-cycle changes. The fingerprint (t2041) handles the "nothing changed" fast path.

5. **Search API error handling** — add Search API patterns to `_pulse_gh_err_is_rate_limit`:
   ```
   'Search rate limit exceeded|search API rate limit|HTTP 422.*abuse detection'
   ```
   On Search API exhaustion: log warning, fall through to per-repo GraphQL calls (degraded but functional). Do NOT abort the cycle — Search exhaustion doesn't mean GraphQL is exhausted.

6. **`_prefetch_repo_daily_cap` stays on GraphQL** — it needs `--state all` + `createdAt`, which search doesn't provide. But for idle repos (t2098), daily cap is already skipped. Net cost: 1 GraphQL call per active repo with open PRs.

### Tier assessment

`tier:standard` — 2 files to modify + 1 new helper, narrative implementation with existing patterns. The normalization function is the only design work; everything else is plumbing.

### Recommendation

Remove `needs-maintainer-review`, add `auto-dispatch` + `tier:standard`. The implementation plan in the issue body + this refinement comment give a worker everything needed. The feature flag (`PULSE_BATCH_PREFETCH_ENABLED`) provides safe rollback.

---

_Self-contained dispatch packet generated by `_dispatch_issue_consolidation()` in `pulse-triage.sh` (t1982). Everything above is sufficient — do not read #18981._

title: t2392: fix(model-availability): treat opencode OAuth tokens as healthy without HTTP probing
body:
## Problem

The `model-availability-helper.sh` probe marks Anthropic as `bad-key` (HTTP 401) whenever the user authenticates only via OpenCode OAuth (the recommended default). This blocks every opus/sonnet-tier dispatch and starves the pulse's deterministic fill floor — 25 candidates enumerated, 0 dispatched on 2026-04-19 ~18:30Z.

## Root cause

`resolve_api_key` at `.agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh:437-444` returns the **raw** OAuth access token (prefix `sk-ant-oat01-`, pulled from `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json`) when it's not expired. `_probe_build_request` at line 767 then sends it as `x-api-key: ${api_key}` to `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models`. Anthropic's `/v1/models` endpoint accepts OAuth tokens only on `Authorization: Bearer`, not on `x-api-key` — result: HTTP 401 `bad-key`.

`resolve_tier opus/sonnet` then returns "No available model for tier" and `dispatch_deterministic_fill_floor` can enumerate candidates but never succeeds. `haiku`/`flash` tiers survive only because they have an `openai/gpt-5.4` fallback; opus/sonnet chains are anthropic-only by design (t1927).

PR #17793 (t1927) added OAuth source 4 to `resolve_api_key` and introduced the `oauth-refresh-available` synthetic marker pattern — but only for **expired** tokens. Non-expired OAuth tokens still flow through to the broken probe.

## Fix

Extend the existing synthetic-marker pattern to all OAuth-type entries in `auth.json`, regardless of expiry. The probe records healthy and skips the HTTP call. Workers still authenticate natively via opencode CLI (unchanged — this is out of the probe path).

See `todo/tasks/t2392-brief.md` for:
- Exact files to modify with line ranges
- Reference pattern to copy (lines 448-456, already-working expired-token branch)
- Three regression test assertions
- Acceptance criteria
- Evidence pointers to `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`

## Scope / out of scope

In scope: opencode CLI OAuth path (primary worker auth). Claude CLI fallback is out of scope — not integrated with OAuth pool, untested for workers, deferred to a separate task.

## Impact

Every aidevops user running opencode without a paid static Anthropic API key hits this (the recommended default setup). Silent dispatch drought. Reported by maintainer in an interactive session; affects all users.

---


<!-- aidevops:sig -->
---
[aidevops.sh](https://aidevops.sh) v3.8.76 plugin for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v1.14.18 with claude-opus-4-7 spent 13h 51m and 107,840 tokens on this with the user in an interactive session.

title: consolidated: auto-rebase or auto-close DIRTY PRs on a periodic pulse sweep
body:
_Supersedes #19779 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Add a new pulse-stage scanner (`pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh`) that detects open PRs with `mergeStateStatus == "DIRTY"` and takes one of three actions based on age, content, and conflict scope:

- **Auto-rebase**: if PR is <48h old AND has real code changes AND only `TODO.md` is conflicting → rebase onto `origin/main`, resolve `TODO.md` by accepting HEAD + re-inserting the PR's task entry at correct chronological position, force-push.
- **Auto-close**: if PR is >7d old AND hasn't had a human push in 3d → close with a comment explaining "superseded by subsequent merges" and link to any issue that remains open for worker re-dispatch.
- **Escalate**: if PR has non-`TODO.md` conflicts and doesn't meet auto-close criteria → post a maintainer-review comment (no destructive action).

Register the new stage in `pulse-wrapper.sh` to run every Nth pulse cycle (~30 min).

## Why

- Interactive users file planning PRs (`TODO.md` + brief file) that go DIRTY within hours of any other `TODO.md` push.
- Workers that complete work but get delayed through the review bot gate age into DIRTY.
- Nobody schedules manual DIRTY-PR triage, so stuck PRs pile up until a session notices them.
- Both actions (rebase if possible, close if stale) are deterministic and idempotent — no human judgment needed in the common case.

Per @marcusquinn: discovered 2026-04-18 during board-clearing session. Three `origin:interactive` PRs (#19754, #19703, #19696) had accumulated merge conflicts and sat unmerged for 1-2 days, each requiring interactive rebase + triage (#19754 and #19703 closed as superseded; #19696 rebased and merged).

## How

### Files to modify

- **NEW:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh` — model on `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` (pulse stage lifecycle: state file, dedup lock, `gh` query loop, comment on action).
- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — register the new stage after the merge pass, gated on an Nth-cycle interval (~30 min).
- **NEW:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dirty-pr-sweep.sh` — test harness with fixtures for all three paths (rebase, close, escalate).

### Detection

```bash
gh pr list --state open --json number,mergeStateStatus,updatedAt,author,labels,files \
  --jq '.[] | select(.mergeStateStatus == "DIRTY")'
```

### Auto-rebase path

Eligibility (ALL must be true):
- `mergeStateStatus == "DIRTY"`
- PR age < 48h
- `author.login == OWNER || labels contains "origin:worker"`
- Conflicting files list (from `git merge-tree --write-tree`) includes ONLY `TODO.md`
- Branch still exists on origin

Action:
1. Create ephemeral worktree for the PR branch.
2. Attempt `git rebase origin/main`. If ONLY `TODO.md` conflicts, resolve via `git checkout --ours TODO.md` + re-insert the PR's task entry (extracted via `git show $commit -- TODO.md`) at correct chronological position.
3. `git push --force-with-lease origin <branch>`.
4. Remove ephemeral worktree.
5. Post PR comment documenting the rebase.

### Auto-close path

Eligibility (ALL must be true):
- `mergeStateStatus == "DIRTY"`
- PR age > 7d
- No human commits in last 3d (check `commits[-1].author.login` against repo maintainer list)
- No `do-not-close` label

Action:
1. Post PR comment explaining closure (template with issue back-link if applicable).
2. `gh pr close --delete-branch`.

### Safety gates

- Dry-run mode (`DRY_RUN=1` env var) prints would-be actions without executing.
- Never rebases a PR with non-`TODO.md` conflicts — escalate to a maintainer-review comment instead.
- Never auto-closes a PR with `do-not-close` label OR linked to an OPEN issue with `parent-task` label.
- Audit log: every action written via `audit-log-helper.sh log dirty-pr-sweep`.
- Idempotent: re-running within 30 min doesn't re-action the same PR (state file tracks actioned PRs + timestamp).

### Reference patterns

- Pulse stage lifecycle (state file, dedup lock, query loop): `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
- Ephemeral worktree management: `worktree-helper.sh`
- PR comment templates: `.agents/scripts/commands/pulse.md`
- `TODO.md` entry manipulation: `task-complete-helper.sh` (for position/format reference)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh --dry-run` lists 0 or more DIRTY PRs with the proposed action (rebase / close / escalate).
- [ ] Test harness `tests/test-dirty-pr-sweep.sh` with fixtures covering all three paths (rebase, close, escalate).
- [ ] Stage registered in `pulse-wrapper.sh` and gated on an Nth-cycle interval (~30 min, not every cycle).
- [ ] Idempotent — re-running within 30 min doesn't re-action the same PR.
- [ ] Never rebases PRs with non-`TODO.md` conflicts (escalates instead).
- [ ] Never rebases `parent-task` PRs.
- [ ] Verification: open a fixture DIRTY PR, run the sweep, confirm rebase succeeds OR close fires per eligibility.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** Architectural decisions (which pulse stage, eligibility windows, rebase conflict resolution heuristics, interaction with existing pulse-merge and dispatch-dedup passes) benefit from deeper reasoning. Multiple files, cross-system coordination, and safety gate design rule out `tier:simple` and `tier:standard`.

## Context & Decisions

- Per @marcusquinn (session origin, 2026-04-18): the initial discovery was during a board-clearing session where three `origin:interactive` PRs (#19754, #19703, #19696) had accumulated DIRTY status. Manual triage took significant interactive time — #19754 and #19703 were closed as superseded, #19696 was rebased and merged. This motivated automating the sweep.
- Per @marcusquinn (comment 2026-04-19): the original issue #19779 was temporarily closed during t2377 (multi-runner enrichment data-loss bug) containment. After the 5-layer defence merged (PR #19876), the issue was reopened with the original brief intact at `todo/tasks/t2350-brief.md`. No spec changes were needed.
- The two-tier approach (auto-rebase for fresh + TODO-only conflicts, auto-close for stale) covers the two distinct failure modes observed in the wild: fast-moving `TODO.md` churn (majority of DIRTY PRs) and abandoned stale PRs that never get triaged.

## Related

- PR #19696 — canonical eligible-for-auto-rebase case (rebased manually 2026-04-18).
- PRs #19754, #19703 — canonical eligible-for-auto-close cases (closed manually 2026-04-18).
- t2377 / GH#19847 — enrichment data-loss fix that temporarily blocked this task.
- `todo/tasks/t2350-brief.md` — original brief file (preserved through data-loss incident).

## Contributors

cc @marcusquinn

title: consolidated: pulse periodic canonical-repo fast-forward + stale worktree cleanup
body:
_Supersedes #19780 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn -->

## What

Add two scheduled maintenance tasks to the pulse:

1. **Canonical-repo fast-forward**: for every repo in `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json`, run `git fetch origin && git checkout main && git pull --ff-only origin main` if the working tree is clean and no active session is mid-edit.
2. **Stale worktree sweep**: for every repo, invoke `worktree-helper.sh clean --auto --force-merged` to drop worktrees whose branch is merged or PR is closed.

Both run on a cadence (~30min — not per-cycle), implemented as a single new pulse stage.

## Why

- Interactive sessions start on canonical main by default. Stale main causes false `pre-edit-check.sh` decisions and requires manual `git pull`.
- Stale worktrees consume disk, clutter `git worktree list`, and confuse the cross-session ownership check (`pre-edit-check.sh` "ownership conflict" logic).
- Both operations are deterministic and safe with the right gates (fail-open on uncommitted changes, respect active-session stamps).
- The agent doesn't need to remember to run these — the harness should.

**Observed scale (per @marcusquinn):** Canonical `~/Git/aidevops` was 2 commits behind `origin/main` at 2026-04-18 session start; `git worktree list` reported 169 total worktrees with ~30 dating from 2026-04-15 (3 days stale) whose branches were already merged.

## Tier

### Tier checklist (verify before assigning)

- [ ] **2 or fewer files to modify?** — No (1 new + 1 edit = 2, but test file makes 3)
- [x] **Every target file under 500 lines?** — Yes (new file, and pulse-wrapper.sh edit is localized)
- [ ] **Exact `oldString`/`newString` for every edit?** — No (new file needs full implementation)
- [ ] **No judgment or design decisions?** — No (safety gates, timeout handling, cadence logic)
- [ ] **No error handling or fallback logic to design?** — No (skip-on-dirty, skip-on-session-active, timeout)
- [ ] **No cross-package or cross-module changes?** — No (pulse-wrapper + new stage + tests)
- [x] **Estimate 1h or less?** — Borderline
- [ ] **4 or fewer acceptance criteria?** — No (8 criteria)

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Well-defined mechanics with a clear reference pattern (`pulse-simplification.sh`), but requires designing safety gates (dirty-tree skip, active-session skip, timeout), error handling, and a test harness — 8 acceptance criteria across 3 files. Not `tier:thinking` because the approach is specified and has a direct template to follow.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh` — new pulse stage combining both operations. Model on `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification.sh` lifecycle (state file, cadence gate, per-repo loop, audit log).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — register the new stage after existing merge/dispatch passes, gated on a ~30min cadence counter.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh` — test harness covering skip-on-dirty, skip-on-session-active, successful fast-forward, and worktree cleanup integration.

### Implementation Steps

1. **Create `pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh`** modelled on `pulse-simplification.sh`:
   - Source `shared-constants.sh` for constants and color fallbacks.
   - Implement `_canonical_fast_forward()`: for each repo in `repos.json` where `pulse: true` and not `local_only`:
     - Skip if `git -C $repo status --porcelain` has output (dirty tree).
     - Skip if `git -C $repo stash list` is non-empty (session in-flight).
     - Check active-session stamps — skip if active session owns canonical.
     - `git -C $repo fetch origin --prune --quiet`.
     - Check `git -C $repo rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main`. If 0, skip.
     - `git -C $repo checkout main && git -C $repo pull --ff-only origin main`.
     - Log via `audit-log-helper.sh log canonical-maintenance`.
   - Implement `_stale_worktree_sweep()`: for each repo, run `timeout 60 worktree-helper.sh clean --auto --force-merged` with per-repo hard timeout (60s).
   - Implement `--dry-run` flag that lists repos needing fast-forward and stale worktrees without mutating state.
   - Cadence state file at `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/pulse-canonical-maintenance-last-run`.

2. **Register in `pulse-wrapper.sh`**: add a cadence-gated call after existing merge/dispatch passes. Use a 30min (1800s) cadence check against the state file's mtime.

3. **Create test harness** `tests/test-pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh`: cover skip-on-dirty, skip-on-session-active, successful fast-forward, and worktree cleanup integration.

### Verification

```bash
# Dry run should list repos and actions without mutating
.agents/scripts/pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh --dry-run

# ShellCheck
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh

# Test harness
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh

# Verify registration in pulse-wrapper
grep -q 'pulse-canonical-maintenance' .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh --dry-run` lists repos needing fast-forward and stale worktrees without mutating state.
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: ".agents/scripts/pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh --dry-run 2>&1 | grep -q 'DRY_RUN'"
  ```
- [ ] Real run fast-forwards canonical main for every clean repo and removes every merged worktree.
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: manual
    prompt: "Run pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh and verify repos are fast-forwarded"
  ```
- [ ] Dirty tree → skip (no stash, no reset).
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh 2>&1 | grep -q 'skip-on-dirty.*PASS'"
  ```
- [ ] Active session stamp → skip (no clobber).
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh 2>&1 | grep -q 'skip-on-session.*PASS'"
  ```
- [ ] Audit log entries for every action.
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "audit-log-helper.sh log"
    path: ".agents/scripts/pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh"
  ```
- [ ] Test harness `tests/test-pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh` covers skip-on-dirty, skip-on-session-active, successful fast-forward, worktree cleanup integration.
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "test -f .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh"
  ```
- [ ] Registered in `pulse-wrapper.sh` on a 30min cadence — not per-cycle.
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "pulse-canonical-maintenance"
    path: ".agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh"
  ```
- [ ] Per-repo hard timeout prevents runaway (60s per repo is a generous default).
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "timeout.*(60|CANONICAL_MAINTENANCE_TIMEOUT)"
    path: ".agents/scripts/pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh"
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- **Cadence choice (per @marcusquinn):** ~30min is sufficient — canonical staleness accumulates over hours, not seconds. Running per-cycle would add unnecessary `git fetch` load.
- **Safety-first skip logic (per @marcusquinn):** dirty tree, non-empty stash, or active session stamp → skip entirely. No stash-pop, no reset, no force. Fail-open is the correct posture for a maintenance task.
- **Per-repo timeout (per @marcusquinn):** 60s hard timeout per repo for worktree cleanup. The existing `worktree-helper.sh clean --auto --force-merged` was observed to spawn 13 runaway processes during manual run (2026-04-18) on a 166-worktree checkout; likely caused by per-worktree `gh pr list` network round-trips. If cleanup consistently hits the timeout, file a follow-up to investigate batching.
- **Reference pattern:** `pulse-simplification.sh` is the cadence-gated template — state file, per-repo loop, audit log. Copy its lifecycle structure.
- **Data-loss incident (historical):** Issue #19780 was temporarily destroyed by a multi-runner enrichment data-loss bug (GH#19847/t2377) on 2026-04-19. The 5-layer defence-in-depth fix merged (PR #19876) and deployed by 05:42 UTC. The brief at `todo/tasks/t2351-brief.md` remained intact throughout. This consolidated issue is the canonical spec going forward.

## Contributors

cc @marcusquinn

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** None — `worktree-helper.sh clean --auto --force-merged` already exists.
- **Blocks:** Cleaner interactive session starts (no manual `git pull`), reduced disk from stale worktrees.
- **External:** None.

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Research/read | 15m | `pulse-simplification.sh` lifecycle pattern, `worktree-helper.sh` API |
| Implementation | 1.5h | New stage script + pulse-wrapper registration + test harness |
| Testing | 30m | Test harness + manual dry-run verification |
| **Total** | **~2.5h** | |

title: t2393: signature footer auto-append on all pulse + worker GitHub comments
body:
## Summary

Extend the t2115 signature-footer pattern from issue/PR **creation** to issue/PR **comments**. Every pulse, worker, and session-lifecycle comment should end with the standard `<!-- aidevops:sig -->` + runtime/version/model/token/time footer produced by `gh-signature-helper.sh footer`.

Today ~50% of our comment paths are unsigned (dispatch dedup ticks, stale-recovery escalations, watchdog kills, tier-escalation diagnostics, terminal-blocker notices, claim/release audit comments). Signing them closes the diagnostic gap so operators — and downstream pulse readers (`contribution-watch-helper.sh`, `backfill-origin-labels.sh`, `dispatch-dedup-cost.sh`) — can always tell which app, aidevops version, model, and session posted each comment.

## Why

Diagnostics. When a comment shows up, we need to know which runtime wrote it, which aidevops version was active, which model ran, and how much time + tokens the session spent. `dispatch-dedup-cost.sh::_sum_issue_token_spend` already parses signatures for cost enforcement — more signed comments = more accurate enforcement.

## How

**Two new wrappers in `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh`:**

- `gh_issue_comment` — thin wrapper around `gh issue comment` that runs `_gh_wrapper_auto_sig` on `--body` / `--body-file` before invocation.
- `gh_pr_comment` — same for `gh pr comment`.

Model on the existing `gh_create_issue` (:1019) and `gh_create_pr` (:1140). Drop the origin-label/assignee logic (creation-only concerns); comments just need the sig.

**Route `_gh_idempotent_comment`** in `pulse-triage.sh:227` through the new wrappers. That single consolidation point covers terminal-blocker, consolidation gate, large-file gate, rebase nudge, and interactive-PR handover comments.

**Sweep all direct callers** across 25+ files (~40-50 individual call sites). Full inventory lives in the brief at `todo/tasks/t2393-brief.md`.

## Reader-side regression audit (pre-implementation, done)

Audited 100+ comment-reading sites, grouped into 5 categories — no regression path identified:

- **Marker-detection readers** (`_gh_idempotent_comment`, `_nmr_application_has_automation_signature`, `_stale_recovery_count_ticks`, `check_terminal_blockers`, `tier-simple-body-shape-helper`) check substring presence of an HTML marker at the TOP of the body; footer appended at the END doesn't affect them.
- **Signature-specific readers** (`_sum_issue_token_spend`, `_scan_backfill_fetch_latest_comment`, `backfill-origin-labels._infer_origin_from_signature`) WANT more signatures — strictly additive win.
- **Body-length / size checks** — only `pulse-merge-carry-forward-diff.sh` truncates at 65KB; footer adds ~200 chars.
- **Terminal-blocker regex** matches specific error phrases ("workflow scope", "ACTION REQUIRED") that never appear in signature footers.
- **Author-login filters** — orthogonal to body content.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `gh_issue_comment` and `gh_pr_comment` exist in `shared-constants.sh` and emit the signature footer when missing, dedup when present.
2. `_gh_idempotent_comment` in `pulse-triage.sh` uses the new wrappers.
3. Every direct `gh issue comment` / `gh pr comment` call in the brief's sweep inventory now routes through the wrappers.
4. `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-auto-sig.sh` extended with comment-wrapper cases and passes.
5. New `.agents/scripts/tests/test-comment-wrapper-marker-dedup.sh` passes, covering both `--body` and `--body-file` paths.
6. `shellcheck` zero-warning on every modified file; existing marker-based reader tests still pass (`test-pulse-nmr-automation-signature.sh`, `test-stale-recovery-escalation.sh`, `test-pulse-labelless-reconcile.sh`, `test-pulse-merge-interactive-handover.sh`).

## Prior art

- PR #19102 / t2115 — initial signature enforcement on `gh_create_issue` / `gh_create_pr`.
- `.agents/scripts/gh-signature-helper.sh` — runtime-agnostic footer generator.

Brief: `todo/tasks/t2393-brief.md` (committed in the implementation PR).

Resolves once merged.

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #19936 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #19936

**Parent issue:** #19936 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** pulse-prefetch: delta fetch always falls back to full sweep due to ${2:-{}} bash expansion bug
**Parent labels:** `auto-dispatch,status:queued,origin:worker,consolidation-in-progress`

> You do **NOT** need to read #19936. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #19936 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #19936:**

```bash
gh issue comment 19936 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 19936 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 19936 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #19936 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #19936** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @marcusquinn

## Parent body (verbatim)

## Description

`_prefetch_repo_prs` and `_prefetch_repo_issues` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch.sh` both start with:

```bash
local cache_entry="${2:-{}}"
```

Bash parses `${PARAM:-WORD}` by terminating `WORD` at the first unescaped `}`, so this expands to "default is `{`" followed by a literal `}`. When `$2` is empty (new-cache path) the result happens to equal `{}`. When `$2` is a non-empty JSON string (the normal delta path, where the caller passes the cached entry from `_prefetch_cache_get`), the local variable becomes the original value plus a trailing `}` — invalid JSON.

Every downstream `jq` call on `cache_entry` then fails. The `.last_prefetch` lookup in `_prefetch_prs_try_delta` / `_prefetch_issues_try_delta` returns empty, the `[[ -z "$last_prefetch" ]]` guard fires, and the helper logs:

```text
[pulse-wrapper] _prefetch_repo_{prs,issues}: delta fetch failed for <owner>/<repo>
  (falling back to full): no timestamp or fetch error
```

Net effect: delta has **never** produced a success since this line was written. Every cycle runs a full `gh pr list --json …` and `gh issue list --json …` instead of the cheap `updated:>=<ts>` search GH#15286 introduced.

## Expected Behaviour

On the second and subsequent pulse cycles (after the first full sweep seeds `last_prefetch` in the cache), `_prefetch_repo_prs` / `_prefetch_repo_issues` should take the delta path and emit log lines like:

```text
[pulse-wrapper] _prefetch_repo_{prs,issues}: delta for <owner>/<repo>: N changed (PRs|issues) merged into cache
```

consuming a fraction of the GraphQL points that a full sweep uses.

## Steps to Reproduce

Direct bash reproducer (no pulse needed):

```bash
f() {
  local x="${2:-{}}"
  printf 'in=%q (len=%d) out=%q (len=%d)\n' "$2" "${#2}" "$x" "${#x}"
}
f slug ''
f slug '{}'
f slug '{"a":1}'
f slug '{"last_prefetch":"2026-04-19T10:00:00Z"}'
```

Output (reproduced on bash 5.2.21):

```text
in=''                                             (len=0)  out=\{\}                                              (len=2)
in=\{\}                                           (len=2)  out=\{\}\}                                            (len=3)
in=\{\"a\":1\}                                    (len=7)  out=\{\"a\":1\}\}                                     (len=8)
in=\{\"last_prefetch\":\"2026-04-19T10:00:00Z\"\} (len=39) out=\{\"last_prefetch\":\"2026-04-19T10:00:00Z\"\}\}  (len=41)
```

The extra trailing `}` is the bug.

End-to-end reproducer (full pipeline, requires a populated `pulse-prefetch-cache.json`):

1. Corrupt the `state_fingerprint` field in the cache for a repo so the cache-hit short-circuit misses.
2. Source `pulse-prefetch.sh` and call `_prefetch_repo_prs <slug> "$(jq -c '.["<owner>/<repo>"]' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-prefetch-cache.json)"`.
3. Observe `cache_entry` arriving at `_prefetch_prs_try_delta` with length = original + 1, `jq -r '.last_prefetch // ""'` returning empty, and the `"no timestamp or fetch error"` log line firing.

## Evidence from a live pulse log

- Total log lines: 220,825
- `"delta fetch failed for"` occurrences: **1,928**
- Delta-success log line (`"delta for .+: [0-9]+ changed (PRs|issues) merged into cache"`): **0**
- `STATE CACHE HIT` (fingerprint-based short-circuit that bypasses the buggy wrappers): 1,205 — these cycles succeed, which is why the cache stays warm and the bug only manifests as wasted quota rather than broken state.
- First failure: log line 98,314 (shortly after `pulse-prefetch.sh` landed).
- Most recent failure: log line 220,477 (current).

## Root cause

Bash parameter expansion grammar: `${PARAM:-WORD}` terminates `WORD` at the first unescaped `}`. Inside the double-quoted string `"${2:-{}}"`, the parser reads `${2:-{}` as the expansion (default = `{`) and treats the trailing `}` as a literal character. This is a well-known foot-gun and `shellcheck` does not currently flag it.

## Affected locations

Primary (actively observed):

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch.sh:692` — `_prefetch_repo_prs`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch.sh:888` — `_prefetch_repo_issues`

Same pattern, latent bug class, worth fixing in the same PR:

- `.agents/scripts/daytona-helper.sh:136` — `local body="${2:-{}}"` passed to `curl -d`. Non-empty caller body → corrupted JSON → API 400, silenced by `curl -f`.
- `.agents/scripts/muapi-helper.sh:686` — `local extra_payload="${1:-{}}"` piped to `jq '. + {…}'`. Non-empty caller payload → `jq` parse error → payload merge fails.
- `.agents/scripts/loop-common.sh:620` — `local evidence="${3:-{}}"`. Has a defensive `jq empty` check at line 623 that catches the invalid JSON and silently resets to `{}` — not a crash, but real caller evidence is discarded.

Git blame on the two `pulse-prefetch.sh` lines points to the Phase 7 extraction commit (`2510f135e`, 2026-04-12). The parent commit's `pulse-wrapper.sh` already contained the identical expansion at the corresponding sites — the extraction preserved the bug byte-identically rather than introducing it. The sibling `_prefetch_{prs,issues}_try_delta` helpers use the correct `"$2"` form, so the bug likely entered when a defensive default was retrofitted to the outer wrappers without realising the bash parser would swallow the closing `}`.

## Recommended fix

Two hygienic options, either is fine:

**A — escape the default braces** (minimal diff):

```bash
local cache_entry="${2:-\{\}}"
```

**B — explicit fallback** (more idiomatic, easier to read):

```bash
local cache_entry="${2:-}"
[[ -n "$cache_entry" ]] || cache_entry="{}"
```

Apply to all five sites listed above. Add a repo-wide grep guard (pre-commit or CI lint) against the literal regex `\$\{[0-9]+:-\{\}\}` to prevent regression.

### Suggested regression test

Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-delta-prefetch.sh`:

1. Call `_prefetch_repo_prs` and `_prefetch_repo_issues` directly with a non-empty `cache_entry` containing `last_prefetch`.
2. Assert that the subsequent `_prefetch_{prs,issues}_try_delta` call does NOT hit the "no timestamp" branch.
3. Assert at least one `"delta for .+: [0-9]+ changed (PRs|issues) merged into cache"` log line is produced.

## Impact

- 100% delta-failure rate on every pulse cycle whose fingerprint-check misses.
- Each failure runs a full `gh pr list --json ...` and `gh issue list --json ...` instead of a bounded `updated:>=<ts>` search — an order-of-magnitude-larger GraphQL cost per repo per cycle.
- The `gh` GraphQL primary quota is 5000 points/hour; with multiple pulse-enabled repos at ~60 cycles/hour, the budget saturates well before the rate-limit-aware paths (GH#18976) can help.
- The intended savings from GH#15286 (delta prefetch) have never been realised, and the further savings proposed in GH#18981 (batched org-level search) compound on top of delta that is currently broken.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.8.76 (latest: 3.8.76)
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: 2.90.0 (2026-04-16)
- **Runtime**: OpenCode (per `log-issue-helper.sh diagnostics`)

## Additional context

Related issues (not duplicates):

- GH#15286 — the `perf: delta prefetch with daily full sweep` initiative this bug breaks.
- GH#18981 — `feat(pulse): batch prefetch via org-level gh search` — open optimisation that assumes delta works.
- GH#19025 — `GraphQL budget optimisation roadmap` — the broader context.
- GH#18976 — `t2097: fail-loud on GraphQL rate limit exhaustion` — complementary, about detecting the symptom.

Bug is not deployed-only: source-of-truth file `~/Git/aidevops/.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch.sh` is identical to the deployed copy. Live pulse is still running with the bug active — evidence preserved.

<!-- aidevops:sig -->
---
[aidevops.sh](https://aidevops.sh) v3.8.76 plugin for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v1.14.18 with claude-opus-4-7 spent 25m and 97,141 tokens on this with the user in an interactive session.

## Substantive comments (verbatim, in chronological order)

### Comment 1 — @marcusquinn at 2026-04-19T16:40:37Z

## Review: Approved

### Pre-Review Context

| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Pre-existing duplicates | None — the search surfaces related work (GH#15286 delta prefetch init, GH#18981 org-level batching, GH#19025 roadmap) but none report this bug |
| Superseded by recent work | None — git log on `pulse-prefetch.sh` for the last 30 days (9 commits) shows no change to lines 692/888; `git blame` confirms the buggy form has been unchanged since `2510f135e` (Phase 7 extraction, 2026-04-12) |
| Framing matches reality | Yes — bash reproducer replicated locally (bash 5.2, output byte-identical to reported). All five cited file:line references match current code on main |
| Current file state matches issue body references | Yes — `pulse-prefetch.sh:692`, `pulse-prefetch.sh:888`, `daytona-helper.sh:136`, `muapi-helper.sh:686`, `loop-common.sh:620` all contain the buggy expansion verbatim |

### Issue Validation

| Check | Status | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| Reproducible | Yes | `bash -c 'f() { local x="${2:-{}}"; ...}'` emits the extra trailing `}` exactly as reported |
| Not a pre-existing duplicate | Yes | |
| Not superseded by recent work | Yes | |
| Actual bug | Yes | Bash parameter-expansion grammar — `${PARAM:-WORD}` terminates `WORD` at the first unescaped `}`. Inside `"${2:-{}}"` the parser reads `${2:-{}` (default = `{`) and leaves the trailing `}` as a literal |
| In scope | Yes | Core pulse infrastructure, direct impact on GraphQL budget |

**Root Cause**: Bash parameter-expansion grammar. `"${2:-{}}"` is not `"${2:-\{\}}"` — the first `}` closes the expansion. When `$2` is non-empty (the normal delta path carrying a cached JSON entry from `_prefetch_cache_get`), the local variable becomes `<original_json>}` — invalid JSON. Every downstream `jq` on `cache_entry` then fails silently, the `.last_prefetch` lookup returns empty, the `[[ -z "$last_prefetch" ]]` guard fires, and delta falls back to full sweep 100% of the time. Cache-hit cycles (fingerprint match) bypass these wrappers entirely — which is why the cache stays warm and the bug manifests as wasted quota rather than broken state.

### Solution Evaluation

| Criterion | Assessment | Notes |
|-----------|------------|-------|
| Simplicity | Good | Two one-line changes at the primary sites plus three at the latent sites; no architecture change |
| Correctness | Good | Both proposed forms (escaped braces OR explicit fallback) are idiomatic and defect-free. I'd lean toward option **B** (`local cache_entry="${2:-}"; [[ -n "$cache_entry" ]] || cache_entry="{}"`) — more readable and easier to grep for later, and `shellcheck` won't be tempted to warn on the escaped braces form |
| Completeness | Good | Reporter identified all five occurrences of the pattern in the codebase; the same bug class at each |
| Consistency | Good | The sibling `_prefetch_{prs,issues}_try_delta` helpers already use the correct `"$2"` form — fix brings the outer wrappers into line with them |

**Alternatives**: Option B (explicit fallback) preferred over A (escaped braces) — same correctness, easier to read and maintain. A repo-wide grep guard (pre-commit or CI lint) on `\$\{[0-9]+:-\{\}\}` is a sensible addition to prevent regression — `shellcheck` does not flag this pattern today.

### Second-Order Effects

| Dimension | Finding |
|-----------|---------|
| Architectural intent | Aligned — restores the intended behaviour of GH#15286 (delta prefetch) which has never actually worked in the `pulse-prefetch.sh`-extracted form. Does not contradict any recent decision; the Phase 7 extraction preserved the bug byte-identically from the pre-extraction wrapper (so latent since before 2026-04-12) |
| Safety gates touched | None — purely a syntactic fix inside internal prefetch helpers. No origin-label, dispatch-dedup, approval-chain, or sandbox-boundary interaction |
| Symptom vs root cause | Root cause fix — resolves the actual parser-level defect rather than papering over the downstream JSON parse errors |
| Ripple effects | (1) GraphQL budget consumption drops materially on every non-cache-hit cycle (order-of-magnitude per cited evidence); (2) log noise from `delta fetch failed for` disappears, replaced by `delta for <slug>: N changed` success lines; (3) `test-pulse-wrapper-delta-prefetch.sh` should get the regression assertions the reporter proposed; (4) `daytona-helper.sh` and `muapi-helper.sh` callers that passed non-empty payloads were silently getting 400/parse errors — fixing those removes a latent failure mode (`loop-common.sh` already has a `jq empty` guard so that one discards real evidence but doesn't crash) |
| Rollback path | Trivial revert — five one-line changes |

### Scope & Recommendation

- Scope creep: Low — reporter correctly scoped to the single bug class across all five sites, plus the regression test extension and a CI grep guard. No unrelated cleanup mixed in
- Complexity: Low (`tier:simple`) — verbatim `oldString`/`newString` available for all five sites, each target file has a single matching line with unique surrounding context, total diff is ~10 lines plus a test extension and a lint rule
- **Decision**: APPROVE — accept the report, convert to an internal task, fix in one PR covering all five sites + the regression test extension + the CI lint rule
- **Labels**: `bug`, `reliability`, `pulse`, `tier:simple`, `auto-dispatch`
- **Implementation guidance**:
